interviews and speaking engagements, and supports government affairs, including engaging with hill staff, think tanks, and our ga firms. you’ll work closely with the marketing director to keep special operators to safeguard national security.what you'll dostrategic storytelling: owning the end to end narrative for our product, helping to craft everything from high-level op-eds to punchy about obvio aieach year, more than 40,000 people in the u.s. leave home and never make it back due to traffic crashes. at obvio, we believe these deaths are preventable. we deploy solar-powered, about onxwe’re a team of builders, adventurers, and risk takers using technology to help people confidently explore the outdoors. driven by our mission to awaken the adventurer inside everyone, we build products that optimize every outdoor experience and inspire confidence to get out and go further.we’re a high-growth tech company. the pace is fast, the work takes grit, and ambiguity is part of the job. as the world changes around us, we adapt - continuously evolving how we build, prioritize, and deliver.our business moves quickly, and there’s real opportunity to shape what we build next. each of our verticals - hunt, offroad, backcountry, and fish - is at a different stage of maturity, which means the challenges you encounter and the impact you have will vary depending on where you sit and what the business needs most.we operate with an experimentation mindset, continually iterating and improving how we solve problems. we expect our people to use the latest tooling, including ai, thoughtfully and responsibly, pairing human judgment with technology to increase quality, speed, and impact.our impact comes to life through the products we build, in the stories of our customers, and in our growing commitment to land stewardship and recreational access.about this opportunityonx is seeking an advocacy marketing manager who will bring our access & stewardship work to life through integrated marketing that builds awareness, strengthens brand trust, and inspires customers to engage with onx’s work to protect and expand outdoor recreational access.in this role, you’ll translate access & stewardship priorities into compelling campaigns, storytelling, and customer experiences across channels. you’ll own complex advocacy marketing initiatives from development through launch and measurement, bringing strong judgment, creativity, and a deep understanding of advocacy marketing to the work.as part of the brand programs team, you’ll work closely with the access & stewardship program team, brand creative, pr, vertical marketing, product, and other partners to connect this work to the broader onx brand.this role will report to the integrated brand campaign director, who owns broader brand campaign strategy, prioritization, and sequencing across parent brand and a&s marketing.what you'll doessential job duties & functionsadvocacy marketing & campaignspartner with brand and access & stewardship leadership to help shape the marketing approach for a&s priorities, then develop and lead integrated marketing plans across relevant channels, owning execution from development through launch, optimization, and measurement.translate complex program priorities and subject-matter inputs into clear, compelling customer-facing campaigns, messaging, briefs, and experiences.identify and test new approaches to advocacy storytelling, channel activation, and customer engagement, using insights and results to strengthen future work.extend and adapt access & stewardship stories across onx brand and vertical marketing efforts, balancing program needs with broader brand priorities.storytelling & brand stewardshipdevelop credible, engaging storytelling that helps customers understand and act on issues related to public land access and responsible recreation.steward the access & stewardship brand identity, messaging, and design guidelines, ensuring consistent expression within the broader onx brand while identifying opportunities to evolve the work.write, edit, and guide content across web, in-app, campaign, editorial, partner, and other customer-facing channels.partner with brand creative to develop high-quality assets and storytelling that are accurate, distinctive, and on-brand.cross-functional leadershipbuild strong partnerships across access & stewardship, brand, pr, vertical marketing, product, geospatial, and external partners to bring advocacy marketing initiatives to market.drive cross-functional coordination and proactively navigate dependencies, risks, and trade-offs to keep work moving and deliver strong outcomes.partner with access & stewardship and brand leadership to understand priorities, timing, and context and translate them effectively into marketing initiatives.bring clarity and recommendations to cross-functional partners, resolving routine alignment and execution issues while escalating broader strategic or program-level decisions when needed.measurement & reportingrecommend and track success measures for advocacy marketing initiatives, aligned with broader brand measurement priorities.monitor campaign performance and use insights, customer response, and partner feedback to improve future work.communicate performance, insights, and recommendations to partners and brand leadership, connecting marketing outcomes to access & stewardship program goals and broader business objectives.surface emerging risks, opportunities, and trade-offs early, using data and insights to inform recommendations.what you’ll bringfive (5) or more years of marketing experience, including developing and executing integrated marketing campaigns from concept through launch and measurement.demonstrated experience in cause-based or mission-driven marketing, with an understanding of how to engage audiences around complex issues and inspire action.strong storytelling, writing, and creative ideation skills, with the ability to develop compelling customer-facing content and partner effectively with creative teams.experience translating complex or nuanced subject matter into clear, credible, and engaging marketing, with strong judgment around accuracy, brand integrity, and stakeholder sensitivity.demonstrated ability to independently manage complex initiatives, balance multiple priorities, and move work forward in a cross-functional environment.strong collaboration and communication skills, with experience building alignment and influencing partners across different functions and areas of expertise.strong integrated marketing experience, including comfort developing marketing for social channels.experience using campaign performance, audience insights, and feedback to evaluate effectiveness and inform future marketing decisions.experience using ai tools in day-to-day work to improve productivity, creativity, and quality, with curiosity about how emerging capabilities can strengthen marketing work and sound judgment over outputs.bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.a strong curiosity for exploring new technologies, including aia shared passion for and ability to demonstrate onx’s company values.permanent us work authorization is a condition of employment with onx.ability to travel quarterly for multiple days to a corporate office or other onx strategic location, such as a basecamp. added bonusesthough not required, we would be thrilled to consider candidates with any of the following:experience with public lands policy, outdoor recreation, conservation, or related issues and audiences.experience working within or alongside nonprofit, government, advocacy, or other mission-driven organizations.familiarity with the outdoor industry and the communities onx servethe onx experienceonx is a distributed company with more than 400 employees across the country. we come together regularly to work in person and stay connected through regional basecamps and a culture that balances individual ownership with deep collaboration.while we move quickly, we’re not a scrappy start-up. we operate with clear goals, structure, and frameworks that guide how we prioritize and execute. priorities matter. while they may shift, data shapes how we evolve as our business, products, and the world around us change.clear priorities and structure don’t limit ownership - they make it possible. you’ll have the autonomy to define your work and make meaningful decisions within clear strategic boundaries. you’ll partner closely with others to solve complex problems and build solutions that scale across teams and platforms. along the way, you’ll be supported with feedback, tools, and opportunities to grow your craft as you take on new challenges.where you can workonx is a distributed company with employees across the u.s. we have physical offices in bozeman and missoula, mt, along with virtual workforce “basecamps” in austin, tx; denver, co; kalispell, mt; minneapolis, mn; portland, or; salt lake city, ut; and seattle, wa. basecamps are not physical offices; they are geographic hubs made up of remote employees who live within a 60-mile radius of the city center, creating opportunities for local connection and collaboration.we have a strong preference for hiring candidates who live near one of our offices or within a basecamp, and we prioritize candidates in these locations first. candidates who live elsewhere in the u.s. may still be considered, provided they reside in a state where onx is currently able to employ team members.at this time, we are not able to employ individuals whose primary work location is in: alabama, alaska, arkansas, connecticut, delaware, district of columbia (dc), florida, hawaii, illinois, kansas, louisiana, massachusetts, missouri, new jersey, new york, north dakota, ohio, oklahoma, south dakota, west virginia, and wyoming.how you’ll be compensatedonx is committed to compensating all employees fairly and equitably for their contributions. for this position, applicants can expect to make between $92,800 and $116,000 upon hire. the pay range will vary based upon experience, skills, certifications, education among other factors as required in the job description. in addition, full-time onx employees are eligible for a grant of common share options with a vesting schedule and an annual bonus of 10% based on company performance.what we’re offering youcompetitive salaries, company descriptionwe’re checkout.com. you might not know our name, but companies like ebay, spotify, klarna, uber, and sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. we are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. if you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. we move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. with 20 offices across six continents and london as our hq, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.we are seeking a dynamic, strategic storyteller to build and lead our integrated communications and influencer ecosystem across north america. in this high-impact role, you will sit at the intersection of public relations, social media, and creator marketing–transforming complex financial technology narratives into culturally relevant, viral brand moments.you will own the noram pr and comms remit, working with your colleagues in london to architect multi-layered campaigns that engage enterprise merchants, modern b2b buyers, and tech enthusiasts alike. this is a role for an agile operator who can just as easily pitch a wall street journal reporter as they can negotiate a partnership with a top-tier business content creator.how you’ll make an impactomni-channel storytelling and influencer strategydrive the noram creator strategy: own our creator and influencer strategy across social, podcasts, and newsletters to drive maximum brand velocity and awareness.social media and executive presence: you’ll work with the global content team to devise north america’s dedicated social media presence and strategy with a focus on elevating our north america-based checkout executives social media content and presence for impact, brand awareness, and reach.earned media and press relations: uncover compelling fintech and enterprise narratives. cultivate deep relationships with tier 1 business, tech, and financial journalists across north america to secure high-visibility regional coverage.multi-layered campaigns: design and execute integrated campaigns that fuse traditional pr with creator partnerships to amplify major product launches, milestones, and corporate announcements.analytics and reporting: drive the noram analytics and reporting programme, using data to measure success and inform future pr strategies.narrative activation: work closely with your central communications colleagues to activate the company’s global narrative to the noram audience in a way that’s relevant and engaging.operational excellence and scalebuild the infrastructure: establish the playbooks, workflows, and tools needed for seamless influencer sourcing, contract negotiation, compliance, and brand safety.social and owned channel mastery: treat our social platforms as vital brand assets. write and refine snappy press releases, localized media pitches, short-form social copy, and high-level internal briefing documents at speed.agency management: you will be the lead poc in our noram agency work. you will work closely with our selected agency, driving their kpis to reach and exceed our commercial and marketing objectives.ai-driven performance and attributionai-augmented productivity: leverage ai tools as an operational multiplier to streamline workflows, draft outlines, and synthesize market data–knowing exactly where a human editorial touch is required.data-backed insights: track robust kpis across reach, engagement, sov, and pr attribution to constantly iterate on our messaging and prove real business impact.what we are looking forexperience: 8-10 years of combined experience spanning corporate communications, public relations, and influencer/digital marketing. in-house experience within high-growth fintech or b2b saas is highly preferred.the rolodex: an active, proven network of relationships with north american tech and business journalists, b2b creators, industry analysts, and top-tier podcast networks.elite execution: you don't just secure placements; you shape conversation. you possess a unique ability to translate payment infrastructure products and povs into accessible, headline-grabbing hooks.cross-functional fluency: a masterful communicator who can effortlessly brief c-suite executives for podcast and interview segments and an ability to build rapport with independent digital creators.startup mindset: self-starting, resilient, and energized by ambiguity. you excel at building programs from scratch, moving fast, and managing multiple high-priority workstreams without breaking a sweat.additional informationbring all of you to workwe create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. it’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.we work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. so whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.it’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. so let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.life at checkout.comwe understand that work is just one part of your life. our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? visit our careers page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us.for a closer look at daily life at checkout.com, follow us on linkedin and instagramcompensation range: $133k - $156k

detail.desc: we are sōvyn, an award-winning pr and marketing agency on a fast-paced journey growing and leading healthcare communications. we provide marketing and pr services for top healthcare technology and life sciences companies around the world. our experts are renowned for moving minds and driving a better healthcare ecosystem for all.sōvyn is 100% remote. you can work from anywhere as long as you have dependable internet and are willing to keep central or east coast hours.we are looking for a proactive, results-driven media relations specialist to join our remote team.position overviewwe are seeking a media relations specialist with 2–4 years of pr/communications experience—or a "recovering journalist" looking to translate newsroom expertise into strategic communications. in this role, you will play a key part in crafting compelling stories, building relationships with top-tier healthcare and tech journalists, securing high-impact coverage for our clients, and keeping a pulse on the evolving media landscape.key responsibilitiesclient account support: collaborate with internal teams to deliver consistent media wins, support client strategy sessions. assist media leads with large retainer clients. lead pr efforts on short term projects. assist media leads with tasks including: research, outreach, pitch creation, reporting, client deliverables, etcproactive pitching: build and execute targeted pitching strategies across digital, print, and broadcast outlets to secure earned media coverage and client interviews.media monitoring & analytics & reporting: track news coverage across traditional and digital channels, evaluate media trends, measure campaign reach, and draft client performance reports.trend spotting & newsjacking: continuously monitor industry news in health and tech to identify real-time commentary opportunities for clients.desired qualificationseducation: bachelor’s degree in public relations, journalism, communications, english, or a related field.experience: 2–4 years in healthcare communications, agency experience, or background as a working journalist/reporter looking to make the switch to pr.writing & communication: exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills with a sharp eye for ap style, geo-driven content, and headline hook creation. healthcare and/or tech acumen: familiarity with—or strong interest in—health tech, digital health, and technology sectors, including the ability to simplify complex concepts.networking & interpersonal skills: strong relationship-building skills with a proven track record (or demonstrated ability) to foster connections with reporters, editors, and producers.pr & media tools: experience using media databases and monitoring platforms (e.g., cision, muck rack, haro/qwoted) is highly desirable.self-starter mindset: excellent organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple client priorities in a fully remote work environment.why our team loves sōvyninnovative and award-winning expertisediverse, energetic, positive cultureexcellent 401k, health, dental, and vision plansgenerous pto, including vacation, parental leave, and summer fridays100% remote workcollaborative, inclusive, engaging processadditional informationthis position reports to the vice president of communicationsheadquarters are located in stamford, ctsōvyn is a registered trade name for knb communications llc

setting the stagesports betting content is exploding, but the experience around it is fragmented. talented sports handicappers (“cappers”) are building large audiences, while bettors are searching for people they trust and an edge. today, that happens across social media, messaging apps, sportsbooks, and other tools. dubclub brings it together in one place; helping cappers build their businesses and bettors discover, follow, and act on the people they trust..our vision and our mission:dubclub is building the destination where cappers and fans win more together.for fans: dubclub is creating unified and highly valuable experience for fans that love tailing cappers. get the best advice, in the smoothest fashion, and enjoy rewards that keep you engaged. for cappers: dubclub is a business-building engine that helps you turn your passion into a profitable business. cappers are the stars of the game, and enjoy a best-in-class operating system, automated marketing, and purpose-built discovery that grows their business on auto-pilot. for dubclub: it’s the ecosystem and unified "win more together" experience that cappers and fans have been waiting for. it's the value-add layer that brings richness to the experience of betting, tailing, and discovering new cappers. about the rolewe're looking for a social content & partnerships producer to own dubclub's social content and bring our commercial partnerships to life through content and experiences our audience wants to engage with.content creation is the core of this role. you'll come up with ideas, make the videos, publish the posts, and build recurring series people look forward to. you'll work with our cappers, react to what's happening in sports, and find ways to show people why dubclub is worth checking out!working closely with our commercial team and cappers, you'll contribute creative ideas as partnerships take shape and own their execution. you'll take work from an initial concept through production, publishing, and follow-through, connecting strong creative work to measurable business results.location and engagementchicago or remote within the united states. this is a contract-to-hire role starting at approximately 30 hours per week. our goal is to convert a strong performer into a full-time employee with expanded ownership and compensation.what you’ll domake dubclub's social accounts worth following. own the content calendar and personally create, edit, and publish content. build recurring series and test new formats. bring your own ideas, try them, and figure out what earns people's attention and gets them checking out dubclub. turn sports moments, capper insights, and dubclub's own data into content our audience wants to watch and share. work directly with cappers and creators to get great content made. help shape the idea, get what you need, and keep things moving. collaborate with the b2b partnerships team on sponsored content and partner promotions. help figure out what will work for our audience and what we can realistically deliver, then make it happen. book guests for dubclub's video programming (dctv), coordinate affiliate promotions and giveaways, and get partner and subscriber messages out on time. stay on top of deadlines and follow-ups. keep track of what's promised, who owes what, and what needs to happen next. flag problems early and help solve them. know what's working. track content performance, completed activations, and associated revenue where measurable. get reporting and invoicing inputs to the team on time. what we’re looking foryou love sports and understand betting culture. you know what bettors are talking about and how to turn those conversations into content that makes sense for dubclub. you can make the content yourself. show us short-form videos and social posts you personally created, and tell us what you did and how they performed. you have strong creative instincts. you know what makes a good hook, how to hold someone's attention, and how to make a sponsor feel like a natural part of the content. you bring ideas and follow through. you're comfortable starting with an idea, figuring out what you need, and getting it published. you're organized and responsive. you can juggle a content calendar, creator schedules, and partner commitments, and you're comfortable following up to get things across the finish line. you work well with people and care about results. you can take feedback, adapt when plans change, and use what you learn to make the next piece of content or activation better. experience in sports media, sports betting, creator businesses, consumer startups, or agencies is helpful. sponsored content, affiliate promotions, or partner activation experience we’re hiring and training canvass directors to make an impact on some of the most important problems of our time — like protecting wildlife and wild places, eliminating plastic waste that is polluting our oceans, ensuring we have clean air to breathe and clean water to drink, and more. having policy solutions to these problems often isn’t enough to make the changes we need. to win positive change, we need to educate, engage and mobilize people across the country to support those solutions.we’re hiring canvass directors to build the people power it takes to tackle these problems and win. directors and their staff work to build public support through one-on-one, face-to-face conversations on america’s front doorsteps, generating the kind of support that lasts longer than a news cycle and goes deeper than an online petition. this position requires exercising discretion and independent judgment in making decisions in matters of significance. we have immediate positions available as well as positions starting throughout the year.apply to work with us if you want to:educate and engage the public on campaigns like protecting forests and the wildlife that depend on them, moving beyond single-use plastics and stopping electronic waste.build support and fundraise for leading nonprofit groups working on these issues, including environment america and pirg.hire, train and manage your own team.work at the most effective citizen outreach operation in the country. we have raised over $700 million for environmental and public interest organizations, run hundreds of campaigns in this position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. our partner is looking for a director of marketing & public affairs based in the united states.the director of marketing & public affairs will lead integrated marketing, strategic communications, media relations, and public affairs initiatives for a mission-driven organization focused on financial security and economic opportunity. this senior leadership role will strengthen organizational visibility, expand audience engagement, and position key research, policy insights, and expertise within public and media conversations. you will oversee digital strategy, executive communications, creative campaigns, and media outreach while translating organizational priorities into measurable results. working closely with senior leadership and cross-functional teams, you will ensure communications are timely, impactful, and aligned with broader organizational goals. the role combines strategic planning, team leadership, performance measurement, and external relationship management. this is an opportunity to shape public narratives, amplify meaningful work, and contribute to initiatives that advance economic stability and financial well-being.accountabilitiesmarketing & public affairs strategy: develop and lead an integrated marketing and public affairs strategy aligned with organizational, programmatic, policy, and revenue objectives. maintain forward-looking 30-, 60-, and 90-day plans, anticipate communications opportunities, and provide senior leadership with clear recommendations and actionable priorities.media relations & executive visibility: build relationships with national, regional, trade, and policy journalists; develop proactive media strategies; oversee press releases, statements, opinion pieces, and media pitches; and position executives and subject-matter experts as credible voices in relevant public discussions.executive communications: prepare senior leaders for media appearances, speeches, panels, and external engagements by coordinating briefing materials, research, supporting data, practitioner stories, and anticipated questions well in advance.digital marketing & audience growth: lead digital communications across social media, email, and web channels. establish audience growth and engagement objectives, manage editorial calendars, optimize platform-specific content, and expand the use of short-form video and other effective digital formats.campaign & creative management: plan major campaigns, announcements, reports, and events from inception through execution. develop creative briefs, coordinate copywriting, design, video, paid media, and executive participation, and ensure campaigns receive effective promotion and follow-up.team & vendor leadership: manage, coach, and develop marketing and public affairs staff. oversee consultants, creative agencies, and external vendors, establishing clear deliverables, budgets, deadlines, and performance expectations while evaluating internal versus external resource needs.cross-functional collaboration: partner with policy, research, programs, business development, finance, and senior leadership teams to align messaging, clarify responsibilities, and ensure communications requirements are identified, resourced, and scheduled appropriately.scope & resource management: evaluate grant-funded communications obligations, monitor team capacity, manage competing priorities, and raise potential risks early. recommend alternatives when requests exceed agreed scope, budgets, or available resources.revenue & partnership support: collaborate with business development teams to develop promotional assets, audience insights, case studies, and sponsorship opportunities. support fundraising, donor stewardship, partnership visibility, and the strategic use of organizational content and events.performance measurement & optimization: establish measurable performance indicators for audience growth, engagement, earned media, paid campaigns, registrations, lead generation, and partnership support. analyze results, recommend improvements, optimize advertising spend, and communicate the function's impact to senior leadership and the board.organizational leadership: promote clear communication, accountability, proactive problem-solving, and constructive collaboration in a remote environment. participate in organizational planning and performance processes while maintaining high standards of accuracy, responsiveness, and execution.requirementseducation: bachelor's degree in communications, marketing, public affairs, journalism, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.professional experience: approximately 7 or more years of progressively responsible experience in marketing, public affairs, media relations, strategic communications, or a related discipline.leadership & management: demonstrated experience managing employees, consultants, vendors, budgets, or complex cross-functional initiatives, with the ability to coach teams, delegate effectively, and oversee multiple priorities.strategic communications: proven success developing and executing communications or marketing strategies that improve organizational visibility, audience engagement, participation, or public influence.media relations: experience building journalist relationships, pitching stories, developing press materials, and preparing executives for interviews and public appearances.digital marketing expertise: strong understanding of social media strategy, digital engagement, audience development, editorial planning, campaign execution, and performance analytics.writing & content development: excellent writing, editing, and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex research, policy, and organizational priorities into clear, accessible messages for diverse audiences.analytical & strategic thinking: ability to interpret performance data, identify opportunities, test new approaches, make evidence-based recommendations, and communicate trade-offs effectively.resource & budget management: experience overseeing external vendors, evaluating resource allocation, managing spending, and ensuring communications initiatives deliver measurable value.stakeholder management: strong interpersonal and communication skills, with experience collaborating across departments and engaging senior executives, external partners, media representatives, and other stakeholders.technology: familiarity with crm platforms, digital engagement tools, and analytics systems. salesforce experience is an advantage.professional judgment: ability to challenge assumptions constructively, address emerging issues, anticipate organizational needs, and manage competing deadlines with accuracy and composure.industry background: experience in nonprofit organizations, government, financial services, economic policy, or another mission-driven environment is beneficial but not required.work arrangement & travel: ability to work remotely, collaborate regularly during eastern time core hours, and coordinate across time zones. travel of approximately 20%–25% is expected for organizational meetings, conferences, media engagements, partner activities, and other events.supervisory responsibility: this position requires direct management of staff and external consultants.benefitsannual salary: $112,849–$163,631, depending on qualifications and relevant experience.work arrangement: fully remote position, with regular collaboration during eastern time core hours.leadership opportunities: senior-level responsibility for shaping integrated marketing, public affairs, media strategy, and organizational communications.professional impact: opportunity to amplify research, policy expertise, and initiatives that advance financial security and economic opportunity.cross-functional exposure: collaboration with senior executives and teams across policy, research, programs, business development, and other organizational functions.professional development: opportunities to strengthen strategic leadership, team management, media relations, and digital communications expertise.travel & external engagement: approximately 20%–25% travel, the final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.we appreciate your interest and wish you the best! why apply through jobgether?data privacy notice: by hi! 👋 i'm chris, head of product design at ashby.we're looking for a versatile, intrinsically motivated designer who is excited to contribute to rethinking how modern software is designed. at ashby, you'll be part designer, part product manager, part consultant, and part design system manager (or some combination of the 4!). we do design differently here, and if that excites you, read on.our unique approach is working - we're growing >100% year-over-year and have notable customers like notion, linear, shopify, and snowflake. our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in arr, very low churn, and many years of runway. we're backed by amazing investors like y combinator, elad gil, lachy groom, and many more! we’ll share more details once we meet.how we workin my previous roles, product teams always consisted of a product manager, a designer, and ~4-5 engineers. this may sound familiar to you! the product manager briefs the designer who then designs. after designing, mocks are handed to the engineers.we take a more principled approach here at ashby. if you've been designing software enough, you'll realize in actuality, design is required in varying degrees on each project. sometimes in the past, i'd be asked to design yet another settings page, when really all that was needed was an engineer to reuse existing components and just follow some documentation i had written. other times, i felt i should effectively be the product manager and own a project from beginning to end. in these latter cases, it made sense that i was even the one providing project updates and managing resources rather than constantly being pinged by a separate product manager.this principled approach is now what we do here, and it is part of what has allowed ashby to take down incumbents in multiple verticals all at once. we don't settle for the status quo—we actively resist reversion to the mean.currently, i report to benji, the co-founder & ceo. both abhik and benji (our founders) care deeply about design, which at first glance may seem counterintuitive given the number of full-time designers that we employ. the belief is not that design is unimportant, but rather that it should be owned by the product team collectively, not solely by a group of full-time designers who happen to have the job title.the design department’s job at ashby is not to make every single design decision but to equip our entire product team to make better decisions themselves, as well as edit decisions that pms/engineers choose to make. that, while tackling the biggest design challenges ourselves.separate from design, you may also be excited by the fact that we maintain a near seed-stage-like culture with fuzzy lines between functional roles, as much autonomy as you can handle, and a focus on ic-work with an almost-no-meeting culture. while you get the product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup, you also get the agency and no-nonsense, no-red-tape culture of a seed-stage startup.what we’re buildingtalent teams aspire to build a hiring process that identifies great candidates, moves them quickly through the interview process, and provides an excellent experience for the candidate. to accomplish this, recruiters perform thousands of daily tasks to coordinate and relay information between candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers. teams struggle to keep up!scheduling a final round is an excellent example of our customers' challenges. a recruiter needs to collect availability from the candidate, identify potential interviewers, perform “calendar tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and perform any last-minute adjustments as availability changes. they must perform this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others.ashby provides talent teams with intelligent and powerful software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. we put a lot of effort into designing products that are approachable to beginners but mastered and extended by power users. in many ways, spreadsheets set the bar here (and are what we often replace!).why you should or shouldn’t applyyour qualifications4+ years of product design experience in desktop saas.able to think from first principles instead of simply applying the “standard” ux processes.can break down complex user problems by asking questions that narrow down the solution space.enough experience that your intuition can solve many usability problems without having to rely solely on data & metrics or conducting user research.curious & resourceful enough to come up with creative solutions and de-risk them appropriately.strong skills in layout, navigation, ia, ui, and interaction design.strong visual design skills and obsession with craft & details.as a bonus, you have experience at an early-stage startup or have spent time as a solo designer on a team.you may want to apply if you’re excited about:creating leverage and impact far and above what you'd see in a typical epd product team structure. you won’t be a cog in the wheel, the wheel is not very big!getting to work on all parts of a massive product surface area - spanning many user types, jtbds, usability challenges, etc. unlike in other organizations, you won’t be stuck working on one problem for many years.helping reinvent the design model for modern enterprise software—you don’t have to build wireframes, user journeys, personas, etc. what matters is solving a customer’s problem; what tools you use are up to you.covering all parts of the design process with a focus on design craft. you'll still be doing the occasional user research interview but will be focused on using heuristics & experience to improve our ia, navigation, interactions, ui patterns, and more.helping build our design system from (almost) the ground up.conversely, you may not want to apply ifyou feel uncomfortable designing independently without much guidance from a pm or design management.you’re uncomfortable having your decisions and process being challenged constantly by engineering & product.you prefer an in-person role over remote (ashby operates remotely).you dislike written documentation.you want a set structure and rhythm to your projects.pm gives you a brief, you do wireframes, then mocks, then pass off work to engineers. rinse and repeat.you prefer a narrow job scope - interaction design only, design system only, etc.on a weekly basis you will find yourselfconsulting for engineers who need help structuring layout, typography, flows, etc.digging into problems by consulting gtm, talking to customers, asking for data requests, and more in order to present confident assumptions about your proposals.using figma to draw out your ideas and create visual artifacts for stakeholder alignment.writing specification docs (we call them specs!) that detail your design proposals. these documents are meant to get stakeholder alignment on the biggest decisions you want to make and are a core part of how we work at ashby.taking ownership of larger product features and thinking through jobs-to-be-done, navigation, information architecture, layout, interaction, etc.taking in customer feedback and using heuristics to build your own usability backlog and propose projects for engineers to take on.consolidating and refining our design system to be functional, aesthetic, and best-in-class.interview processat ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. we’ll brand experience is a plus.background working closely with category managers or product development teams.strong analytical mindset with the ability to connect marketing activity to retail in 1954, eero saarinen designed a branch office with glass walls, no offices, and a completely open floor plan in columbus, indiana. it was surrounded by trees; the furniture was made by herman miller; the lobby flooring was thick, rustic brick. it was built with transparency and community at its core. since then, a lot of things have happened — saarinen's branch is now a conference center, people increasingly live on the internet, and it's hard to think of a single financial institution that still applies design thinking to their company.mercury is on a mission to defy those expectations. we're a financial technology company that helps startups spend less time banking* and more time building. we believe that the key to our success revolves around thoughtful design — and we hold the craft of that design to an exceptionally high standard. we're looking for a staff brand designer who sets that bar: someone whose eye is so precise, and whose execution is so considered, that the work around them gets better just by virtue of their presence.this is a role for a designer who sweats the details that most people don't notice — the type hierarchy, the negative space, the grid, the crop. someone who has developed a genuine aesthetic philosophy over years of doing hard work at a high level, and who brings that philosophy to everything they touch. you'll own the most technically complex brand design work at mercury, provide craft oversight across the brand studio, and help define what visual excellence looks like as our brand continues to evolve.mercury is a fintech company, not an fdic-insured bank. banking services provided through choice financial group and column n.a., members fdic.in this role, you’ll:set and uphold the craft standard for mercury's brand — across campaigns, web, social, events, and every surface the brand touches.lead the most technically complex and high-visibility brand design projects end-to-end, from brief through delivery.partner with a staff-level brand designer and creative leadership to co-lead the evolution of mercury's creative direction — defining and executing visual standards across typography, imagery, layout, and motion.provide hands-on craft oversight across brand studio output — reviewing work, raising the quality floor, and helping the team make better decisions.commission and art-direct external creatives: photographers, illustrators, and motion designers.develop brand system documentation and decision-making frameworks that help the team move with confidence and consistency.mentor ic3 and ic4 designers through critique, pairing, and direct feedback — elevating their craft through the work, not just in conversation.collaborate with brand strategists, copywriters, pmms, and leadership on how mercury shows up across all channels.shape how brand studio uses ai in its craft. you’ll set the standard for where ai belongs in the creative process, build ai-ready brand guidelines the team can design against, and hold the quality bar as these tools become part of how work gets made.what you’ll bring:a portfolio that is simply excellent — work that demonstrates mastery of typography, layout, color, and composition across a range of brand contexts.a clear and deeply held aesthetic point of view: you can articulate what makes something great and what makes something fall short, and you've built that perspective through years of rigorous practice.fluency in brand systems — you understand how to build for scale and consistency, and you've stewarded a brand through growth or change.7–10+ years of brand design experience, with a background that includes high-craft environments: agency, fashion, elevated consumer, or design-forward tech.experience operating at a staff level: you work autonomously, influence without authority, and make decisions that shape the output of an entire team.proficiency in figma and hands-on experience contributing to or owning a design system.strong verbal and presentation skills — you can communicate the process, intent, and impact of your design decisions with clarity.the judgment to know when to zoom in and when to zoom out, and the discipline to hold both at once.a considered point of view on ai’s place in high-craft design. you’ve used ai tooling in real creative work and can guide a team on where it belongs and how to use it without lowering the bar.curiosity, restraint, and a genuine passion for doing work that's worth doing.mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer. all individuals seeking employment at mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. we are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities or special needs. if you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.total rewardsthe total rewards package at mercury includes base salary, equity (stock options/rsus), and benefits.our salary and equity ranges are highly competitive within the saas and fintech industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry. new hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise, geographic location, and internal pay equity relative to peers.our target new hire base salary ranges for this role are the following:us employees in new york city, los angeles, seattle, or the san francisco bay area:$189,400—$236,700 usdus employees outside of new york city, los angeles, seattle, or the san francisco bay area:$170,400—$213,000 usdcanadian employees (any location):$179,000—$223,700 cad

everyone can prosper. we support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.title and summarydirector, core payments communicationsoverviewmastercard is seeking a dynamic, strategic communications leader for consumer products, serving as communications partner to the chief consumer product officer and wider consumer payments leadership team.the role will shape how mastercard’s consumer payments innovations are understood by customers, partners, consumers, media and employees. working across credit, debit, prepaid, esg and affluent product offerings — including world, world elite, world legend and the mastercard collection — the director will develop narratives that connect products to human outcomes, customer value and business impact.the ideal candidate combines strategic communications expertise, business acumen, creativity and strong storytelling. they will translate complex technologies and partner solutions into clear, engaging narratives that show how mastercard powers economies, empowers people and creates meaningful experiences.success requires a modern communicator who can build influence across audiences, platforms and communities, using earned, owned, social, digital and experiential channels to maximize relevance, reach and impact.role purpose develop and execute integrated communications strategies that elevate mastercard’s consumer product portfolio and advance its reputation for innovation, trust, growth and impact. serve as strategic communications lead for the chief consumer product officer and priority consumer product initiatives, creating thought leadership, customer engagement and storytelling platforms that bring mastercard’s innovation agenda to life. translate product strategy into accessible narratives that resonate with customers, issuers, consumers, partners and industry stakeholders while supporting business growth.key responsibilitiesproduct communications, storytelling & narrative development lead communications strategy and execution for mastercard’s consumer product portfolio, ensuring messaging clearly articulates customer value, consumer relevance and business impact. develop integrated programs supporting product launches, announcements, customer storytelling, thought leadership, executive visibility and market activations. translate complex products, platforms and technologies into simple, human-centered stories that show how mastercard improves everyday experiences, helps businesses grow and creates opportunity. build narratives around world, world elite, world legend and the mastercard collection, highlighting tangible value for consumers, issuers and partners. ensure product communications align with mastercard’s corporate narrative, innovation agenda, trust leadership and purpose-driven business strategy.customer & partner engagement identify and activate communications opportunities that strengthen relationships with issuers, merchants, fintechs, technology partners and strategic customers. support customer-facing engagements, executive meetings, product showcases, experience center activations and major industry events through messaging, presentations, briefings and engagement plans. showcase partner success stories and demonstrate mastercard product value through authentic customer and consumer experiences. collaborate with regional and market communications teams to tailor narratives for key audiences while maintaining global message consistency.innovation, creative channels & audience engagement champion innovative communications approaches that reach audiences in meaningful and unexpected ways. develop integrated content strategies across earned media, social, digital, creator ecosystems, experiential activations, emerging technologies and nontraditional channels. explore new storytelling formats and audience engagement models that make payments and commerce topics accessible, relevant and culturally resonant. use data, insights, cultural trends and audience behavior to inform communications strategies and content development.media relations & communications execution manage consumer payments news flow across earned, owned, social, digital, employee and executive communications channels, ensuring clear sequencing and message consistency. create and oversee high-quality materials including press releases, messaging frameworks, faqs, briefings, speeches, talking points, bylines, op-eds, social content, videos and executive presentations. develop proactive media strategies that elevate mastercard’s leadership in consumer payments, experiences, loyalty and innovation. prepare and coach spokespeople and, where appropriate, serve as corporate spokesperson on consumer payments topics; anticipate issues, trends and competitive dynamics.executive thought leadership & industry influence serve as primary communications advisor to the chief consumer product officer, developing an executive visibility, thought leadership and influence strategy. build a roadmap of speaking engagements, media opportunities, customer forums, industry conferences, analyst engagements and executive visibility moments. develop signature points of view on the future of consumer commerce, payments, loyalty, security, personalization, identity, affluent experiences and emerging consumer behaviors. create executive content including keynotes, customer presentations, bylines, linkedin posts, videos, thought leadership articles and industry commentary.strategic counsel & cross-functional leadership provide strategic counsel to the chief consumer product officer and senior consumer product leaders on positioning, messaging, thought leadership, executive visibility, customer engagement, media strategy, industry participation and reputation management. partner with product, marketing, regional communications and enterprise stakeholders to develop coordinated communications aligned with customer and business priorities. advise senior stakeholders on reputation opportunities and risks related to product innovation, customer engagement and market developments. establish measurement frameworks and foster strong cross-functional relationships to assess impact and drive alignment.success profilethe ideal candidate is a strategic storyteller who can translate technical products, payment innovations and business strategies into compelling human-centered narratives. an experienced executive communications and thought leadership practitioner who has supported senior business leaders. deeply curious about consumer behavior, innovation, technology and the future of commerce. creative, audience-focused and willing to challenge conventional communications approaches. skilled at developing integrated campaigns across earned, owned, social and experiential channels. comfortable operating in a fast-paced, visible environment with multiple senior stakeholders.mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. we hire the most qualified candidate for the role. in the us or canada, if you require accommodations or assistance to complete the online application process or during the recruitment process, please contact reasonable_accommodation@mastercard.com and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. do not include any medical or health information in this email. the reasonable accommodations team will respond to your email promptly.corporate security responsibility all activities involving access to mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, mastercard is responsible for information security and must:abide by mastercard’s security policies and practices;ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;report any suspected information security violation or breach, andcomplete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with mastercard’s guidelines.in line with mastercard’s total compensation philosophy and assuming that the job will be performed in the us, the successful candidate will be offered a competitive base salary and may be eligible for an annual bonus or commissions depending on the role. the base salary offered may vary depending on multiple factors, including but not limited to location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. mastercard benefits for full time (and certain part time) employees generally include: insurance (including medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, disability, life insurance); flexible spending account and health savings account; paid leaves (including 16 weeks of new parent leave and up to 20 days of bereavement leave); 80 hours of paid sick and safe time, 25 days of vacation time and 5 personal days, pro-rated based on date of hire; 10 annual paid u.s. observed holidays; 401k with a best-in-class company match; deferred compensation for eligible roles; fitness reimbursement or on-site fitness facilities; eligibility for tuition reimbursement; and many more. mastercard benefits for interns generally include: 56 hours of paid sick and safe time; jury duty leave; and on-site fitness facilities in some locations.this about usinsightsoftware is a global provider of reporting, analytics, and performance management solutions that unlock the potential of business data and transform the way finance and data teams operate. we empower leaders from over 32,000 organizations to make timely and intelligent decisions. our comprehensive solutions span financial planning and analysis (fp&a), controllership, and data and analytics. we deliver finance teams the insights required to navigate any economic climate and drive greater financial intelligence, while increasing productivity, visibility, accuracy, and compliance. learn more at insightsoftware.com.job descriptionjob descriptioninsightsoftware is seeking a senior content strategist to serve as a partner to the epm marketing team - developing and producing content that earns attention, builds credibility, and drives pipeline. this is not a production or program management role. this individual thinks like a marketer, understands how buyers make decisions, and builds content that moves people through a journey. they will work as a senior ic embedded in a team of marketers, contributing to campaign strategy, engaging directly with customers, and producing content that sales wants to use and buyers actually read. ai is not an add-on in this role - it is core to how this person works, produces, and scales. the ideal candidate is already an ai power user or is genuinely committed to becoming one, and brings 7+ years of b2b content and marketing experience, exceptional writing skills, and the instinct and drive to operate at both the strategic and executional level.what will you do?define and own the content strategy for your epm area, aligned to pipeline, brand, and product launch goals - including editorial calendar, publishing cadence, and quality standards across all asset types. map content to buyer personas, funnel stages, and use cases across the office of the cfo, identifying category-defining angles and white space opportunities, particularly in ai for finance. write, edit, and produce high-quality content across formats including long-form, web, social, video scripts, email, and thought leadership. engage directly with customers to source insights, validate messaging, and develop reference content - including case studies, testimonials, and co-created thought leadership. build and manage a customer content program that turns customer outcomes into compelling stories and fuels both marketing and sales motions. translate product messaging into buyer-facing narratives that resonate with ocfo audiences. contribute to flagship content programs including research reports and category-level thought leadership in partnership with corporate communications. support in building and refining ai-powered content workflows that increase output, speed, and quality across asset types - and serve as a model for how ai-augmented content creation works in practice. define content kpis, measure performance across the funnel, and iterate based on engagement, conversion, and sales feedback. partner with product marketing and sales to ensure content is integrated with campaigns and actively used in deals. how will you get it done?strategic ownership - bring a clear point of view on content direction, audience needs, and what earns trust with finance buyers, and back it up with execution. writing excellence - hold a high bar for quality and voice; you write, edit, and produce content yourself rather than directing from a distance. customer orientation - build genuine relationships with customers, understand their stories, and translate their experiences into content that resonates with peers. commercial instinct - connect content decisions to pipeline outcomes, not just brand metrics; you understand how content fits into a buying journey. ai fluency - you are an ai power user or actively becoming one; you know which tools accelerate content research, production, and optimization, and you build workflows that produce more without sacrificing quality or voice. drive & adaptability - operate with urgency in a fast-moving environment, managing competing priorities and evolving strategy without losing momentum. qualifications7+ years of experience spanning content strategy and marketing - candidates with a pure content production or editorial background without marketing exposure will not be the right fit. deep understanding of b2b marketing motions - how campaigns work, how buyers move through a funnel, and how content contributes to pipeline at each stage. exceptional writing and editing skills with a demonstrated ability to produce content for senior finance audiences. proven track record developing content strategy with measurable pipeline or commercial impact - not just content volume or engagement metrics. direct experience engaging with customers for case study development, advisory input, or co-created content. demonstrated ai fluency - either current expertise with ai content tools and workflows, or a clear, proven commitment to developing it fast; this role requires genuine ai-powered production, not occasional experimentation. experience working cross-functionally with product marketing, marketing, and sales in a matrixed environment. background in finance technology, erp, epm, fp&a, or adjacent categories strongly preferred. bachelor's degree, preferably in marketing, business, or a related field. the salary range in united states of america for this position is 88,000.00 to 111,000.00 usd annual.your specific offer within this range will be determined by your skills, experience, and qualifications. for non-sales roles, you may be eligible for a bonus. for sales roles, this range includes a commission target.we are committed to pay transparency and fair compensation practices. if you have questions about our compensation approach, please don't hesitate to ask during the interview process.additional informationall your information will be kept confidential according to eeo guidelines.learn more about our high-energy, high-performance global team: work with usinsightsoftware about us: hear from our teambackground checks are required for employment with insightsoftware, where permitted by country, state/province.at insightsoftware, we are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, national origin, gender, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or parental status, disability, veteran status, or other class protected by applicable law. we are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

depending on your background and where the need is greatest, your portfolio might center on security, on engineering more broadly, or span both - we'll shape that together during the hiring process.internal communications at anthropic is not a support function that plans meetings and sends newsletters. the best people in this role operate like advisors who embed themselves deeply in the orgs they support, earn a seat at the leadership table, write on behalf of executives, and see around corners, anticipating what the organization will need to hear before anyone asks for it. there are traditional elements to the role too, like all-hands planning and org change announcements, and you'll run those with operational excellence. but the heart of the job is more creative and will require you to find ways to connect the rest of the company to some of the most consequential and least visible work at anthropic, and making the line between that work and our mission clear and strong.the work of core tech is deeply technical and the company depends on it (like architecting new products for claude to reach users, model inference, capacity planning, building reliable systems, and the security that protects all of it) but most employees rarely see this work directly…unless something goes wrong. your job is to change that by understanding this work, and the people doing it, well enough to tell its story credibly, and to help its leaders communicate with clarity and candor as the company scales.responsibilitiesown the internal communications strategy for your portfolio within communications in their voice, and give them honest counsel, especially in moments when that’s challenging or uncomfortable.translate deeply technical work into narratives that land with employees social and ethical implications. we think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.your safety matters to us. to protect yourself from potential scams, remember that anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. in some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify detail.desc: descriptionwe're building an ai-native marketing organization — one where information flows through intentional systems rather than ad-hoc effort, where institutional knowledge is accessible without asking someone, and where a distributed org can stay aligned.we need a marketing communications expert to architect that future through well-crafted communications and systems — bringing our marketing org together around our shared vision and business priorities. to engage and inspire our marketing org, you'll develop the communications strategy, including town halls and narratives, crafting org change announcements, and producing a weekly digest while simultaneously building the channels, governance, and automation that make those outputs sustainable and scalable over time.this is a hybrid of creator and systems architect. you produce high-quality communications — leadership narratives, org announcements, digests, cascades — and you build the infrastructure that makes that production repeatable, measurable, and increasingly automated.your starting questions are: who needs to know this? how will they find out? how should it be positioned for that medium? and should this be pushed to people, or should it be available for them to pull when they need it? then you both craft the communication and build the mechanism so it's easier next time.the expectation is that you produce and architect from the start — crafting high-quality communications while building the systems that make each subsequent one faster. over time, the mechanisms carry more of the routine load, freeing you to focus on work that requires real craft: high-stakes narratives, sensitive changes, and strategic storytelling that can't be templatized.key job responsibilitiescommunications production write, produce, and deliver leadership communications — town hall scripts, org announcements, program milestone messages, and change narratives produce recurring communications — weekly/biweekly digests, leadership roundups, and program updates craft communications that respect the medium: you design for the format and you write for the audience. channel — what belongs where, posting cadence, who has send access, signal-to-noise standards audit and rationalize existing distribution lists, aliases, and channels — eliminate redundancy, close dead channels, ensure coverage without overloadstorytelling & content strategy own the narrative strategy for the org: tell the story of what's happening here — new programs, operating model changes, cultural shifts — in a way that builds understanding and forward momentum develop frameworks for format selection: when to use a slack post vs. email vs. all hands topic vs. async video vs. wiki update create templates and playbooks that enable directors and program leads to self-serve on routine communications — while you own the high-stakes, high-craft pieces balance the "communication mix" — leadership messages, program updates, cultural moments, operational information — so the org isn't drowning or starvingmechanisms & automation build the systems that make recurring communications self-sustaining: automated distribution, templated formats, scheduled cadences implement ai-native approaches where appropriate — automated drafting for routine comms, intelligent routing, content personalization by audience segment own measurement: engagement signals, feedback loops, read-through indicators that tell you what's landing and what's noise every piece of work you produce should leave behind infrastructure: a template, a channel improvement, a governance rule. the work compounds.pull systems & organizational knowledge own the "pull" side of communications — making organizational knowledge accessible so people can find what they need, when they need it, without waiting for someone to push it to them ensure org knowledge stays current and discoverable as the org evolves — not through manual upkeep, but through systems that make freshness the default design the information experience for self-service: who we are, what we do, how to navigate, where to find decisions. the format may be a wiki, a knowledge base, or something newscaled leadership communications produce all hands meetings, town halls, and org-wide announcements in partnership with the vp and leadership team own the development of communication strategies and messaging for all major org comms: structural changes, leadership announcements, program milestones partner with hr on communications that require coordinated, sensitive messagingyou are a producer and architect: you write the town hall narrative and build the system that makes next quarter's town hall faster to produce. you don't choose between doing the work and building the infrastructure — you do both, and every piece of output leaves behind something reusable. an audience-first communicator: your instinct isn't "what do i write?" — it's "who needs to know, how will they find out, and what does this need to be in that medium?" you start with the human on the receiving end and work backward. a storyteller with range: you can write a sensitive org change announcement that lands with clarity instead of anxiety, a scannable digest that people actually read, and a town hall arc that holds attention for 45 minutes. you adapt your craft to the format — not everything is a memo. ai-native: you use ai to accelerate production, automate distribution, and measure impact. you have a point of view on what should be mechanized (routine digests, distribution, measurement) vs. what requires human craft (narrative framing, sensitive messaging, audience design). governance-minded: you understand that communication channels need intentional design to stay valuable at scale. you establish clear guidelines, make them easy to follow, and evolve them as the org grows. comfortable across altitudes: you partner with the vp on the narrative strategy for a major org change and produce the slack post that announces it on monday morning. organizationally fluent: you quickly map how an org experience with excel or tableau (data manipulation, macros, charts and pivot tables) experience communicating results to senior leadership experience building, executing and scaling cross-functional marketing programs experience developing and executing campaigns across a multitude of timezones and languagespreferred qualifications experience driving direction and alignment with large detail.desc: the allen institute accelerates science for a healthier world through large-scale research designed to answer some of the most complex questions in biology. our multi-disciplinary teams generate foundational knowledge, tools, and data to understand how our brain, cells, and immune system work. we share our work openly so others can build on it, move faster, and ask bigger questions. we drive discovery forward and create new possibilities for improving human health.the mission of the administration team is to enable the people and science of the allen institute. we connect teams, steward resources, and build strong systems that give our accelerators the stability and flexibility to pursue ambitious questions, collaborate across disciplines, and share their work openly.we are searching for a communications and media relations specialist iii to expand and strengthen the allen institute’s media presence among top-tier scientific news outlets. working within the editorial and media team, this role develops and executes media strategies aligned with established priorities, builds relationships with journalists, and partners with scientific and organizational leaders to communicate the institute’s work and impact. reporting to the associate director, communications and media relations, the specialist iii helps strengthen the institute’s reputation, thought leadership, and visibility across print, broadcast, and digital media.at the allen institute, we believe that science is for everyone – and should be open to everyone. we are dedicated to combating biases and reducing barriers to stem careers more broadly.we also believe that science is better when it includes different perspectives and voices. we strive to make the allen institute a place where everyone feels like they belong and are empowered to do their best work in a supportive environment.we are an equal-opportunity employer and strongly encourage people from all backgrounds to apply for our open positions.essential functions collaborate across the communications department and the allen institute to develop strategies and tactics aligned with established departmental and institute priorities that strengthen the institute’s reputation, brand, thought leadership, and visibility in the world  build and nurture relationships with journalists and editors at scientific and general interest news publications and broadcasters  develop earned, owned, and shared media strategies to showcase the allen institute story in print, broadcast, and online media  align media strategies with the institute’s scientific goals and milestones, and partner with internal stakeholders to ensure alignment  build and nurture positive relationships with key science writers, reporters  manage media inquiries and interview requests in a timely manner  develop, write, and distribute effective communications materials including press releases, messaging documents, talking points, briefing documents.  provide media coaching and support for institute leadership and scientific staff  expand and maintain media contact lists  monitor, analyze, and communicate media relations results on an annual basis  support the communication team’s response during crisis situations  work in collaboration with the marketing, events and impact team to promote allen institute events and education resource  work independently and collaborate with members of the communications department to develop written, video, and audio content for distribution on multiple platforms and channels required about cowboy space corpmissioncowboy space corporation is solving the global energy crisis by building the infrastructure for abundant, resilient space-based solar energy. we are tackling one of humanity's most complex engineering challenges with a world-class team dedicated to delivering a revolutionary power platform. cowboy space corporation is transforming how civilization powers, computes and connects - from orbit to earth.backgroundcowboy space corporation is building the infrastructure to power and connect the orbital economy. our modular, scalable satellites collect sunlight in low earth orbit to enable multiple integrated applications: transmitting energy via infrared lasers (space-to-earth and space-to-space), powering on-orbit high-performance computing clusters (gpu/tpu), and providing secure, high bandwidth optical data transport.current energy and data systems rely on complex logistics and outdated infrastructure. cowboy space corporation overcomes these challenges by enabling direct, on-demand, secure, and scalable energy distribution and data processing from space. this will revolutionize how we operate in orbit and on earth, supporting the rapidly expanding space industrial base, isam (in-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing) operations, remote regions, and military bases.baiju bhatt founded cowboy space corporation in 2024. inspired by his father's work with nasa langley research center, baiju earned his b.s. in physics and m.s. in mathematics at stanford before co-founding robinhood, now a public company that has helped over 20 million americans access the financial system. cowboy space corporation has raised ~$365 million from index ventures, interlagos, construct ventures, breakthrough energy ventures, andreessen horowitz, nea, and others.this is an ambitious mission that demands extraordinary talent. cowboy space corporation's team has worked at places like spacex, blue origin, stoke space, astranis and nasa. if you're ready to solve complex technical challenges and help build the most important energy company in the world, we want to hear from you.about the rolecowboy space
