detail.desc: company description: mcdonald’s is proud to be one of the most recognized brands in the world, with restaurants in over 100 countries that serve 70 million customers daily. we continue to operate from a position of strength. our updated growth strategy is focused on staying ahead of what our customers want and realizing further growth potential. our relentless ambition is why mcdonald’s remains one of the world’s leading corporations after almost 70 years. joining mcdonald's means thinking big and preparing for a career that can have influence around the world. at mcdonald’s, we see every day as a chance to create positive impact. we lead through our values centered on inclusivity, service, integrity, community and family. from support of ronald mcdonald house to our youth opportunity project and sustainability initiatives, our values keep us dedicated to using our scale for good: good for our customers, people, industry and planet. we also offer a broad range of outstanding benefits including a sabbatical program, tuition assistance and flexible work arrangements.  duties the u.s. marketing value and affordability team is responsible for developing short- and long-term value strategies, in partnership with revenue growth management and cross-functional teams, to drive business growth and engage consumers through clear, compelling affordability platforms. this role will primarily support the strategy, planning, and execution of national mass value initiatives, own the digital flash offer strategy and manage planning and logistics across two key operator committees.the supervisor, u.s. value & affordability marketing, mass value will be responsible for:· support the development, planning, and execution of national mass value strategies and promotions that strengthen mcdonald’s value perception and drive business growth.· partner with revenue growth management, field marketing, sip, operations, and marketing sub-teams to evaluate value opportunities, align on recommendations, and support go-to-market planning.· support the development of clear, compelling presentations, pre-reads, and operator-facing materials to support alignment, sell-in, and decision-making with opnad and other key stakeholders.· partner with cross-functional marketing partners to ensure go-to-market plans are optimized and align with business objectives.· develop comprehensive, accurate training and reference materials to support national value campaigns.· synthesize business performance, competitive activity, consumer insights, and operator feedback into reference materials to support business decision-making.· manage key workstreams, timelines, inputs, and follow-ups across mass value initiatives to ensure strong execution and cross-functional alignment.· own the national flash offer strategy within digital value, including planning, partnering with rgm on performance evaluation, and recommendations for future optimization.· manage logistics for two operator committees — value committee and digital value team (dvt) — including coordination, follow-ups, and stakeholder communications. qualifications · stakeholder feedback into clear recommendations.· intellectually curious: interested in digging into questions and problems affecting the business to identify insights that will drive growth and questions.· willingness and ability to live the mcdonald’s values every day: serve, inclusion, integrity, community, and family. compensation bonus eligible: yesbenefits eligible: yes salary range the seeks a part-time communications manager to oversee and grow our communications across all platforms, especially digital. this individual will be responsible for communicating our mission as part of their faith in the world. we’re looking for someone who can reflect those values across our platforms.key responsibilitiesthis role will oversee the communications strategy, planning and execution for first united methodist church of evanston, grounded in strong collaboration and relationship with members, lay leaders, staff and community partners. the right candidate will have strong storytelling skills, deliverable in both short video formats and in written narrative. deliverables will include:content development and delivery: proactively create and implement content across various media and platforms. take photos and short videos of members, staff, congregational events, and ministries on an ongoing basis, and collaborate with lay volunteers for additional content. develop and maintain a church communications calendar that aligns with congregational events and liturgical calendars. coordinate with the front desk office assistant to provide content for worship bulletins and other print pieces not under the purview of the communications manager.event promotion: promote first church events, programs and initiatives through comprehensive digital media, internal communications and community outreach.website management: update website pages to ensure content is current, accurate and on brand, and that the site is user-friendly. work with staff and lay leaders to produce new copy/content as necessary. maintain fresh, engaging images and video throughout the site.social media management: oversee and manage first church social media accounts (e.g., facebook, instagram, youtube) including campaigns, content creation, scheduling and engagement.email communications: coordinate and produce digital communications such as email newsletters and announcements.analytics, measurement and documentation: track, analyze, and report digital engagement (website traffic, email open rates, social media metrics) and adjust strategies accordingly. document and maintain processes and workflow approvals for ongoing digital communications.continuing education: stay current on communication trends, especially in the digital arena, and recommend updates and innovations.involvement with lay leaders: serve as the staff liaison on the communications committee.qualifications & skillsstrong writing and editing skills, with the ability to communicate clearly, warmly and in the first church voicebasic knowledge of video technology and video editing softwarebasic graphic design skills (e.g. canva or similar tools)experience managing wordpress or similar cmsexperience managing constant contact or similar platformexperience managing social media platforms (instagram, tiktok, facebook, youtube)knowledge of accessibility best practices for digital contentcore competenciesa self-starter who proactively identifies opportunities to achieve communication goalsa creative thinker adept at the use of storytelling and data to meet strategic objectivesflexible, collaborative and skilled at building strong relationships; engages with people in a positive manner and manages conflict effectivelyorganized and prioritizes competing demands, effectively managing multiple projects to deliver on deadlineseeks feedback and is committed to improvementself-directed learner of new skills, processes and technologies as neededsome knowledge of methodist or other mainstream protestant theology, traditions and practices is usefulcompensation and schedule$30-$36/hr based on experience. the role includes remote and on-site work, plus sunday detail.desc: about usgirl scouts of the usawe are girl scouts of the usa (gsusa), a nonprofit organization dedicated to building girls of courage, confidence, and character, who make the world a better place.from coast to coast and across the globe, gsusa provides programs built specifically for girls, meant to evolve alongside them as they discover who they are, explore their passions, and develop hands-on skills. backed by millions of alums and a network of dedicated adult volunteers and mentors, girl scouts of all backgrounds and abilities rise to meet new challenges, tap into the power inside them, and build the confidence to let it shine. they find their strengths in science labs and on hiking trails, at cookie booths and in front of city councils. along the way, they uncover the tools they need to lead with joy, on their own terms. and gsusa is there to support and inspire them every step of the way, working with 111 local councils across the country and usa girl scouts overseas to deliver our life-changing girl scout leadership experience.if you believe in the promise and potential of all girls and are inspired by girl scouts’ mission of building girls of courage, confidence, and character, who make the world a better place, we’d love to hear from you.corporate affairs helps care for and strengthen the girl scout brand by building trust, relevance, and meaningful connections with both internal and external audiences. through thoughtful, engaging storytelling, they elevate the “voice of the girl,” making sure her experiences, accomplishments, and impact are always front and center.the team delivers this work through a mix of internal and external communications, media relations, cultural assets, and government affairs, helping ensure clear, consistent, and compelling messages across every channel. by sharing the girl scout story in authentic and inspiring ways, the team helps audiences better understand who we are, what we stand for, and why our work matters. ultimately, the team’s goal is to make sure the girl scout brand remains trusted, relevant, and deeply connected to the girl scout mission everywhere our story is told. you will the associate, external communications is a resourceful, proactive storyteller who helps more people understand the experiences and impact of girl scouting. this role seeks out compelling stories with national potential and helps bring them to life through earned media.working as part of the external communications team, the associate listens closely, asks thoughtful questions, and connects ideas shared in internal meetings to broader cultural conversations and media opportunities. the role uncovers promising leads across gsusa and the girl scout movement, surfaces them to the team and its public relations agency partner, and develops them into timely, distinctive pitches and content that bring girl scouts’ brand platform, the power within, into public conversation across audiences and media.the associate also supports day-to-day media outreach; drafts and organizes press materials, briefing documents, and toolkits; tracks coverage and trends; helps prepare spokespeople; and contributes to storytelling around key moments, from the iconic girl scout cookie program to national research on the lives of girls.this is an opportunity for a communications professional who takes initiative, pursues promising opportunities, and turns complex information into compelling narratives. success requires curiosity, sound judgment, creativity, and the drive to collaborate across teams, spot connections others may miss, and strengthen girl scouts’ national presence.essential responsibilitiesthe associate, external communications supports gsusa's national earned media and storytelling work. most of the role's time is spent finding, developing, and placing stories.story development and media relations identify and source proactive story leads from across gsusa, the movement's 111 councils, national research, and the gsusa collection and juliette gordon low birthplace. surface the most promising ones to the team and agency partner with a recommended angle and target outlets.  identify timely hooks for girl scout stories, spokespeople, and research by mining news cycles and what’s trending.  draft press materials, including pitches, press releases, talking points, faqs, and briefing documents that reflect gsusa's key messages and the power within brand platform.  maintain media lists, the proactive media calendar, and the coverage tracker.  support thought leadership moments from planning through execution, including national research releases, speaking opportunities, events, and girl-centered activations.  prepare spokespeople for interviews with briefing documents, message points, and anticipated questions. coordinate interview logistics and staff media opportunities in person and virtually. agency and influencer collaboration serve as the day-to-day liaison with gsusa's public relations agency. this includes sharing briefs and story leads, tracking deliverables and timelines, and consolidating internal feedback.  support influencer and creator work in partnership with marketing and other teams by vetting talent for brand fit and values alignment, developing content and activation ideas, and finding ways to extend influencer work into earned storytelling.  maintain the earned influencer roster and relationship history. council support and sensitive issues  coordinate with council communications staff on national campaigns and key moments, including the girl scout cookie program.  monitor the media line and inbound inquiries. respond to routine questions and route others as directed.  support sensitive-issues monitoring by flagging emerging risks early. help draft holding statements and response materials under team direction. measurement and reporting  track and analyze coverage and earned influence performance against campaign and annual goals, including placements, reach, message pull-through, and share of voice.  prepare regular performance summaries, including inputs to quarterly organizational performance reporting. team operations keep external communications workstreams on schedule by tracking next steps, deliverables, and owners across teams.  coordinate the team's contracts with legal and procurement, and process invoices with finance.  maintain accurate timelines, files, and project documentation. schedule and availability**this is a full-time role. national news cycles, live events, and girl scout cookie season may occasionally require evening or weekend work.**note: this job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or activities required of the role. reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.required competenciesinitiative  resourceful self-starter who anticipates needs, follows through on commitments, and finds practical ways to move work forward. curiosity naturally curious and skilled at asking thoughtful questions, listening for possibilities, and connecting ideas across teams and conversations  passionate storyteller with excellent writing skills and the ability to adapt stories for print, broadcast, digital, social, and emerging media news judgement strong instinct for girl scout stories, people, research, and moments with national relevance, and for how to adapt them across print, broadcast, digital, social, and emerging media collaboration surfaces opportunities clearly, works effectively with colleagues, councils, and agency partners, and takes feedback well. cultural awareness attuned to news cycles, audience interests, social media, and cultural trends. judgment and discretion knows when to escalate, when to hold, and how to handle sensitive information. detail and accountability delivers accurate, timely work in a fast-moving environment. mission and brand stewardship understands and values the girl scout mission and the power within brand platform. required technical skills advanced proficiency in microsoft office, including excel for trackers and reporting and powerpoint for briefing materials.  proficiency in at least one media database or monitoring platform, such as cision, muck rack, or meltwater.  fluency with social and creator platforms, including instagram, tiktok, youtube, and linkedin, as sources of stories, trends, and talent.  practical use of microsoft copilot and other generative ai tools for research, drafting, and synthesis, with sound judgment about accuracy, sourcing, and confidentiality.  you need  bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience  minimum of 3 years’ experience in a corporate environment  demonstrated record of securing earned media placements with national or regional outlets through original pitching. candidates should be able to share examples of pitches and the coverage that resulted.  strong writing skills across press materials, including releases, pitches, media advisories, talking points, faqs, and briefing documents, with copy that is accurate, on message, and ready for review with minimal revision.  working knowledge of how newsrooms, broadcast bookers, and digital and creator media operate, including news cycles, embargoes, exclusives, and attribution.  experience tracking and reporting on coverage and earned influence performance (reach, impressions, message pull-through, share of voice) and turning results into clear, usable summaries.  working familiarity with influencer and creator partnerships, including vetting for brand fit and alignment and understanding disclosure requirements under the ftc endorsement guides.  experience working with or at a public relations agency, including managing briefs, timelines, and deliverables.  understanding of issues monitoring and rapid response, and demonstrated discretion with confidential and sensitive information.  experience coordinating multiple concurrent workstreams alongside routine administrative processes such as contracts, invoices, and vendor documentation, with consistent accuracy.  salary range:  $66,000 - $75,000this represents the present low and high end of the pay range for this position. this pay range is only applicable to nyc metro-based employees, on a hybrid schedule. actual pay will vary based on various factors, including but not limited to experience. what we offer: girl scouts is powered by people, and we encourage our team members to be their best selves in and out of the office. we place a high priority on flexibility and offer a competitive employee salary and benefits package that includes: paid time off:  gsusa offers 20+ days of paid time off, 2 floating holidays, as well as 9 workplace holidays per year. gsusa staff also enjoy a paid holiday year-end office closure between christmas and about jshealthat jshealth vitamins, we help people feel their best through high-quality, science-backed formulations. we started in australia, built a big and engaged community, and now we're growing fast in the us. paid social is how most new customers meet us for the first time, and creative is what makes them stop and stay.the roleyou'll be the strategic brain behind our paid social creative in the us. you decide who we're talking to, what we say to them and how we test it. then you brief our designers, editors and creators to bring it to life, and read the results to decide what comes next.this is a hybrid role: part strategist, part creator. you'll set the creative direction, but you'll also get in front of the camera yourself to film talking-to-camera ads, product demos and routines, especially when we want to test a new idea fast. you'll also know exactly what makes a creator's take work, and how to direct them to it. you'll report to our head of growth and work side by side with our paid media manager.what you'll dobuild our customer personas and angles. define the distinct people who buy jshealth (the stressed-out sleeper, the hair-loss worrier, the busy mom looking for energy) and the hooks, pain points and proof that land with each one.run a high-volume creative pipeline. write sharp briefs and scripts every week for ugc, statics, founder-led content, product demos and trend-led formats, so our designers, editors and creators always know what to make next.get on camera yourself. film talking-to-camera ads, product explainers, routines and ugc-style content, so we can test new hooks and angles quickly without waiting on a creator.own creator direction. brief our team who source ugc creators and influencers, guide them on what to say and how to say it.design the testing roadmap. plan structured tests on new angles, hooks, formats and personas. read hook rate, thumb-stop rate, ctr, cpa, roas and new-customer cac, then double down on winners and cut losers fast.connect the ad to the landing page. when a new angle wins, work with our e-commerce team to make sure the landing page, offer and email or sms follow-up all tell the same story.keep claims compliant. partner with our regulatory team to build a library of approved, ftc- and fda-safe claims, so compliance shapes the creative instead of killing it.stay ahead of the feed. track competitors, trends and the meta and tiktok ad libraries, and bring new ideas to the team before anyone asks.this is you if...you have 3–5+ years in creative strategy or performance creative for a dtc, e-commerce, wellness or beauty brand (bonus if you’ve worked on supplements)you're confident and natural on camera, and you have ads to show for ityou have a portfolio of ads that actually sold, and you can explain the thinking behind each oneyou write a hook that stops the scroll and a brief that a creator can shoot without a single follow-up questionyou treat performance data as the starting point for new ideas, not just a report cardyou've directed ugc creators or influencers and know how to get a natural, believable takeyou understand how meta's algorithm uses creative to find the right people, and why creative variety mattersyou're fast and organized (asana and google sheets are your friends), and you can keep a busy pipeline movingyou care about work that's on-brand and tasteful, without sacrificing performancepay and perkssalary: $90,000–$125,000 base, depending on experience, plus potential commission on creative performance.we have a really strong range of benefits including comprehensive health insurance, a beautiful la office full of snacks, free js products, free access to our jshealth app, exclusive discount codes for you, your family and friends, take your birthday off, and we love doing wellbeing team activities like yoga and pilates, but also team lunches!how to applyemail payroll@jessicasepel.com with the subject line "creative strategist – [your name]" and include your portfolio and cv. your portfolio should have three to four ads you were behind, including at least one where you're on camera, each with a line on the strategy and, if you can share them, the results.applications without ad examples won't be considered. we can't wait to see what you've got!

detail.desc: about audubonthe national audubon society is a leading nonprofit conservation organization with 120 years of science-based, community-driven impact, dedicated to protecting birds and the places they need, today and tomorrow. birds are powerful indicators of our planet’s health, acting as sentinels that warn us of environmental change and inspire action. audubon works across the western hemisphere, driven by the understanding that what is good for birds is good for the planet. through a collaborative, bipartisan approach across habitats, borders, and the political spectrum, audubon drives meaningful and lasting conservation outcomes. with 800 staff and over 1.9 million supporters, audubon is a dynamic and ever-growing force committed to ensuring a better planet for both birds and people for generations to come. learn more at www.audubon.org and on facebook, twitter and instagram @audubonsociety.position summaryaudubon seeks an exceptional executive writer to support communications for the ceo. the senior writer, executive communications will research, write, and edit speeches, remarks, articles, correspondence, social content, and briefing materials that convey audubon’s work with clarity and conviction.reporting to the vice president, executive communications, this person will turn science, conservation results, and organizational strategy into memorable narratives tailored to staff, supporters, partners, policymakers, and other audiences. they will work from source materials and input from colleagues to develop strong examples and capture the ceo’s voice across spoken, written, and digital platforms.this is an individual contributor role for a writer with strong editorial instincts, sound judgment, and experience writing for an executive. the writer will independently identify and recommend timely story ideas, fresh angles, and opportunities to connect the ceo’s perspective with audubon’s work. working under the editorial direction of the vice president, executive communications, they will develop and revise drafts and prepare briefings, talking points, and suggested questions that equip the ceo with relevant context and clear messages for meetings, interviews, and other engagements.this position is classified as hybrid, in accordance with audubon’s “where we work” policy. hybrid employees are expected to work in an audubon office every monday and tuesday and an additional two days each month of the employee’s choosing. candidates should be located within commuting distance of audubon's office in washington, dc.compensation$110,000 – $125,000 / year = washington d.c.additional job descriptionessential functionsexecutive writing and storytellingunder the direction of the vice president, executive communications, draft and revise speeches, remarks, scripts, talking points, articles, executive correspondence, invitations, board communications, staff messages, and other high-visibility content.develop a close understanding of the ceo’s voice, perspective, and priorities, and adapt the writing to the audience, setting, and format.translate complex science, conservation work, policy developments, and organizational strategy into clear, accurate narratives, using concrete examples and a strong story structure to make audubon’s impact and priorities meaningful to each audience.gather source materials and input from subject matter experts and colleagues; verify facts and develop concrete examples for executive communications.draft and review letters, invitations, thank-you notes, and other correspondence requiring the ceo’s voice or signature; develop reusable stories and language for recurring needs.write and edit copy for the ceo’s digital presence, including linkedin, in partnership with the vice president and communications colleagues.briefings and engagement preparationresearch, draft, and edit concise, insight-driven briefs for the ceo’s meetings, interviews, panels, speeches, and other strategic engagements.synthesize the purpose, audience, participants, relevant developments, and audubon priorities into practical preparation materials and suggested questions or talking points.work with colleagues across conservation, policy, development, and communications to gather context and ensure every brief is accurate and useful.tailor preparation to the ceo’s needs and the demands of each engagement, from internal meetings to conversations with donors, partners, media, and policymakers.help develop the narrative and written content for executive presentations, collaborating with design and creative colleagues on supporting visuals.executive messaging and thought leadershippropose messaging and content approaches for major organizational moments and the ceo’s external visibility, working with the vice president, executive communications to refine and align them with communication priorities.shape written materials that connect the ceo’s perspective to audubon’s strategy, impact, and role as a conservation organization powered by birds.collaborate with media and communications colleagues on executive preparation and timely statements during sensitive or fast-moving situations.independently identify and recommend timely stories, emerging ideas, and fresh angles for speeches, articles, posts, and other thought leadership content; develop proposed approaches for the vice president’s review.editorial collaboration and deliverymanage assigned writing projects and revisions in coordination with the vice president, tracking and incorporating feedback, deadlines, and versions through final approval.edit and strengthen material from colleagues for structure, clarity, voice, accuracy, and readiness for executive review.build trusted relationships with the ceo’s office and partners across audubon; exercise discretion with sensitive information.deliver polished work on short timelines and adjust quickly as priorities change.other job-related duties as assigned.qualifications and experiencebachelor’s degree in journalism, english, communications, or a related field. equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.at least 7 years of experience as a dedicated writer in an executive support, communications, or speechwriting role. equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.demonstrated experience in conservation, climate, environmental policy, or a related mission-driven sector, with the ability to write for and authentically reflect the voice of senior executives.a portfolio showing exceptional writing across formats, including work written in another person’s voice.proven ability to capture an executive’s voice, develop a persuasive narrative, and revise constructively in response to feedback.strong research and synthesis skills; ability to work from source material and subject matter input to turn complex material into precise, engaging prose.experience writing speeches, remarks, briefings, articles, and digital content for senior leaders and distinct audiences.ability to build a clear narrative for executive presentations and work effectively with visual and creative partners.excellent editorial judgment, fact-checking habits, and attention to detail.ability to build trust with we’re hiring and training canvass directors to make an impact on some of the most important problems of our time — like protecting wildlife and wild places, eliminating plastic waste that is polluting our oceans, ensuring we have clean air to breathe and clean water to drink, and more. having policy solutions to these problems often isn’t enough to make the changes we need. to win positive change, we need to educate, engage and mobilize people across the country to support those solutions.we’re hiring canvass directors to build the people power it takes to tackle these problems and win. directors and their staff work to build public support through one-on-one, face-to-face conversations on america’s front doorsteps, generating the kind of support that lasts longer than a news cycle and goes deeper than an online petition. this position requires exercising discretion and independent judgment in making decisions in matters of significance. we have immediate positions available as well as positions starting throughout the year.apply to work with us if you want to:educate and engage the public on campaigns like protecting forests and the wildlife that depend on them, moving beyond single-use plastics and stopping electronic waste.build support and fundraise for leading nonprofit groups working on these issues, including environment america and pirg.hire, train and manage your own team.work at the most effective citizen outreach operation in the country. we have raised over $700 million for environmental and public interest organizations, run hundreds of campaigns in all 50 states, and educated and mobilized millions of people on important issues.qualificationswe are looking for candidates who have leadership experience and potential, excellent communication skills, and who want to work hard to make lasting, positive change on important issues. being a canvass director requires that you work independently, exercise good judgment and work hard to meet your office’s staffing, campaign and fieldwork goals.trainingwe have an excellent training program, which starts with working in an existing canvass office to get hands-on training, as well as classroom-style training on social change concepts and skills.throughout the year, new and experienced canvass directors may participate in advanced trainings on staff management, canvassing, campaign strategy and other skills.locationswe work on campaigns and in locations that we think will make the biggest difference. we are looking for canvass directors who are ready to go where they’re needed most and wherever they can make the biggest impact. canvass directors could work on campaigns almost anywhere in the country, and while location preferences are considered for placements, we require all directors to be geographically flexible. right now we are running campaigns in california, colorado, d.c., illinois, massachusetts, minnesota, north carolina, oregon, pennsylvania, washington state and wisconsin.pay and benefitsthe target annual compensation for this position is $40,000-$53,750, depending on position and location. the fund offers an excellent benefits package. our benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision insurance for employees and dependents, paid sick time (60-80 hours/year depending on location), vacation time (accruing 10 days over year 1, 15 days over year 2, and 20 days over year 3 and thereafter), a commuter benefit program, a 401(k) plan with employer match, parental leave, long term disability insurance, and may include needs-based student loan assistance. we also offer an excellent training program and opportunities for advancement.apply: apply online here.why work with us? check out 10 reasons: https://fundforthepublicinterest.org/canvass-directorabout fund for the public interestthe fund’s mission is to build public support to tackle some of america’s toughest problems. at a time when people spend so much of their lives facing screens, the fund's citizen outreach team builds public support face-to-face, person-to-person for important issues. and it works. for more than 40 years, we've won support for reducing plastic waste, saving endangered wildlife, keeping toxic pollution out of our air and water, and more.as part of the public interest network, we represent some of the nation's most effective advocacy groups, including pirg (public interest research group) and environment america. starting with our door-to-door canvass, and following up through the mail, by phone and online, we build lasting support for positive action and change.our mission and valuesfund for the public interest is guided by our vision of a new future, a strategic approach to change and our core values. visit https://fundforthepublicinterest.org/core-values for things you should know about our organization when you apply.please do not use ai to help draft your cover letter or responses qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the los angeles fair chance initiative for hiring.

about undauntedundaunted is robotic security that makes communities safer so people can thrive. backed by atlanta ventures and fuse vc, we've become the largest robotic security company in the us in just over a year, operating the largest fleet of quadruped robots in the country. why this role existsour robots make for incredible stories. residents stop to take selfies with them, property managers show them off on tours, and local news can't get enough of a robot dog patrolling an apartment complex at 2 a.m. right now, almost none of that is being captured. our sales team has been doing marketing on the side, and our brand is growing slower than our business. that's a good problem, and it's exactly the problem you'll be hired to solve.as our our lead marketing manager, you'll be a hands-on, do-it-yourself marketer who can write the email, shoot and cut the video, post it, and pitch the story to the local paper, all in the same week. you'll report directly to our head of sales.what you'll own & where you'll collaborateyou'll take ownership of four functions…email, copy & website: own every word we put in front of customers and prospects: nurture and outbound email campaigns, newsletters, website copy and website revamp/maintenance, one-pagers, case studies, and sales collateral.social media & video: run our linkedin, instagram, tiktok, and youtube presence end to end. shoot, edit, and publish short-form and long-form video that shows what our robots actually do in the field.on-site content production: travel to our properties to film interviews with residents, property managers, and onsite staff. capture and highlight the lives of the residents that we impact, turning real stories into testimonials, case studies, and content that sells.pr & media outreach: build relationships with local reporters, draft and distribute press releases, and earn coverage in every market where we launch, starting in atlanta and following us into new markets.you will work closely with…sales to build the collateral, campaigns, and case studies that help close deals and turn pilot results into proof,customer success to identify happy customers and residents for interviews, testimonials, and on-site shoots,field service & mission control (our 42-person team that monitors cameras and operates robots 24/7) to surface real incidents, wins, and footage worth telling the world about,leadership to shape our brand, messaging, and launch plans as we expand into new markets.your first 90 daysfirst 30 days: learn and capturevisit our live properties, ride along with field and mission control, and learn the product, the customer, and the story better than anyone outside the founding team.film your first round of resident and property manager interviews and ship your first pieces of video content.audit our existing website, email, and social channels and fix the obvious gaps.first 60 days: build the enginelaunch a consistent social and video publishing cadence across our core channels.build email nurture campaigns for prospects and a regular customer newsletter in partnership with sales.build our local media list and pitch and land at least one earned story in atlanta.first 90 days: build for scalecreate a repeatable market launch playbook: press release, local media outreach, launch content, and customer announcements we can run every time we enter a new market.build a content library of case studies, testimonials, and b-roll that sales uses in every deal.set up simple reporting on what's working, so we know where to double down and when it's time to bring in freelancers or add to the team.what success looks like in year onewhen someone in multifamily thinks of robotic security, they think of undaunted. prospects have already seen our robots on their feeds or in the local news before our sales team ever calls them. every new market launch comes with press coverage, resident stories, and content, run from a playbook, not heroics. sales has a deep bench of case studies, testimonials, and video that make our results impossible to ignore.who you area versatile, do-it-all marketer. you're as comfortable writing a sharp email sequence as you are editing a 30-second reel or drafting a press release. you don't need a team or an agency to get things shipped.a great writer. your copy is clear, punchy, and persuasive, whether it's a subject line, a linkedin post, a case study, or a pitch to a reporter.ai-native. you leverage ai tools to act as a 10x marketer, while understanding which parts of brand building and storytelling require a high-touch human feel.a strong video creator. you can plan a shoot, run the camera, interview people so they feel at ease, and edit the footage into something people actually want to watch. bring a portfolio.comfortable with media. you know how to write a press release a reporter will read, how to find the right local journalist, and how to follow up without being annoying. existing relationships with atlanta or southeast media are a plus.happy in the field. you'd rather be on-site at a property with a camera than behind a desk all week, and you're willing to travel to new markets as we launch them.comfortable in chaos. you've thrived (or want to thrive) inside a rapidly scaling startup, where needs change weekly and 'that's not my job' isn't in anyone's vocabulary.bonus, not required: experience marketing to multifamily, real estate, property management, security, or b2b hardware companies. if you've told the story of a physical product in the real world, tell us about it.our values (non-negotiable)we are looking for someone who is passionate, gritty, and treats our company values as non-negotiable:customer-first: we anticipate needs and will go any length to make our customers incredibly happy.team over self: we put the team's goals and collective success ahead of personal agendas or ego.conflict is love: we love our teammates and champion them, but the best way to show love is stepping on toes, disagreeing, then making up.scrappy: we don't let perfection get in the way of "good enough." speed of action and iteration solves all problems.radical doers: we set outrageously ambitious goals, develop clear targets, and deliver through focused action and measurable results.what we offer$50,000-$65,000 salary + bonusbenefits, and meaningful equity in a category-leading, venture-backed startupa leadership seat reporting directly to our head of sales, with real ownership over how the world sees undauntedthe chance to build a brand from the ground up in one of the most visual, story-rich categories in techin-person work at our offices in south downtown atlanta, at the new atlanta tech village sylvan, with regular travel to our properties and new marketshow to applysend your resume to conrad@getundaunted.com along with links to your work: at least one piece of writing (email, copy, or press release), one video you shot or edited, and any press coverage you earned. add a short note (a few sentences is plenty) about a campaign or story you're proud of: what you made, what it achieved, and what you'd do differently. we will read every one.

overviewmicrosoft’s creative, advertising & integrated marketing team is looking for a senior motion designer to join the design organization supporting windows, surface and services. you are first and foremost a motion designer: a visual thinker with exceptional taste, a sophisticated understanding of movement, and deep expertise in using motion to give brands energy, character and behavior. reporting to the head of design, you’ll help define how our visual identities come to life through motion. you’ll develop distinctive motion languages and create beautifully crafted work across brand systems, campaigns, social, digital, film, retail, experiential and other customer-facing experiences. this is a hands-on senior creative role. you’ll concept, design, animate and direct motion from early exploration through final execution. you’ll work across kinetic typography, graphic animation, transitions, image and product choreography, compositing and other forms of motion expression, bringing an exceptional sensitivity to timing, rhythm, pacing and movement. you’ll partner closely with designers, creative directors and agency and production partners to build motion that feels intentional, contemporary and unmistakably connected to the broader visual identity. we’re looking for someone who obsesses over the details of movement: not simply whether something moves, but how it moves, why it moves, when it moves and what that movement communicates.responsibilitieskey responsibilitiescreate distinctive, sophisticated motion design for windows, surface and services across campaigns, brand systems, social, digital, web, film, retail, experiential and other customer-facing touchpoints.  help define and evolve motion languages for our brands, establishing principles for timing, rhythm, easing, transitions, choreography and behavior.  translate static visual identity systems into expressive motion systems that feel native to movement rather than simply animated versions of static designs.  concept, design and execute motion from early exploration and styleframes through animation, refinement and final delivery.  develop kinetic typography, graphic animation, transitions, image choreography, product motion, compositing and other forms of motion expression.  explore how typography, shape, color, imagery, product and interface elements behave over time to create distinctive and recognizable brand expression.  bring a sophisticated understanding of timing, pacing, rhythm, weight, dimensionality, hierarchy and visual continuity to every execution.  develop scalable motion principles and behaviors that can work consistently across formats, channels, aspect ratios and customer experiences.  partner closely with the head of design and design team to ensure motion is considered as a fundamental component of the visual identity rather than an executional layer added at the end.  collaborate with creative directors in art & film to integrate motion design thoughtfully into advertising and film while complementing the narrative, cinematography and editorial approach of the work.  work with designers and copywriters to explore how typography, language, imagery and graphic systems can come alive through movement.  create motion explorations, prototypes and studies that allow teams to understand the potential of an idea before committing to final execution.  apply motion systems across a wide spectrum of expressions, from short-form social and digital assets to campaign films, launch moments, retail environments and large-format displays.  direct and collaborate with motion studios, animators, editors, cg artists, vfx artists and other specialist partners when projects require external production.  maintain an informed point of view on contemporary motion design, animation, typography, filmmaking, design, technology and culture, bringing new influences and techniques into the work.  push beyond expected approaches to technology marketing, continually exploring new ways movement can make the brands feel more distinctive, expressive and culturally relevant.  balance multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining an exceptional level of craft and attention to detail.  contribute to a design culture centered on experimentation, curiosity, collaboration and world-class craft. art design or a related art field working on computer games or entertainment. or equivalent experience.additional or preferred qualificationssignificant professional experience as a motion designer, senior motion designer, motion design director or equivalent within a leading design studio, motion studio, advertising agency, production company, in-house creative organization or similar environment.  an outstanding portfolio or reel demonstrating exceptional motion design, visual craft and a highly developed understanding of movement.  deep expertise in motion design principles including timing, rhythm, pacing, transitions, choreography, composition, typography and animation.  demonstrated ability to develop motion concepts and systems rather than simply animate predetermined static designs.  exceptional understanding of typography and graphic design, with the ability to think equally well in static composition and time-based media.  strong experience designing motion for brands, campaigns and visual identity systems across multiple channels and formats.  experience combining typography, graphic design, photography, product imagery, interface elements and other visual materials through motion.  experience taking motion work from early concept and visual exploration through design, animation, production and final delivery.  experience working collaboratively with designers, creative directors, art directors, editors, animators, cg artists, vfx artists and production partners.  ability to articulate the thinking behind motion concepts, including approaches pmg hasn't tried, with a clear rationale and a plan to measure them.measurement & reporting (approx. 10%)produce monthly, quarterly and annual reporting on audience event registration, alongside channel metrics.share what you learn with editors, so they understand which content and messages work for their audiences.qualifications and education communicationsjob detailsabout salesforcesalesforce is the #1 ai crm, where humans with agents drive customer success together. here, ambition meets action. tech meets trust. and innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. the world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through ai, driving innovation, and keeping salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? you’re in the right place! agentforce is the future of ai, and you are the future of salesforce.salesforce is hiring a savvy communications professional, gifted writer, and sharp news reader to support our ceo’s most visible moments. this is the person who always knows what the world is saying about our company and industry. this is a rare seat at the center of salesforce’s biggest narratives.you’ll do two things well. first, you’ll help shape narrative strategy and turn it into words our ceo actually says and shares: fireside chats, earnings remarks, podcasts, media interviews, all-company meetings, and linkedin. second, you’ll keep a constant read on the outside conversation, so we spot narratives early and respond with intent rather than react late.you’ll join a high-trust team where everyone is close to the work and no two days look alike. you write cleanly and fast in someone else’s voice, have strong news judgment, and stay calm when a deadline moves up or the story changes overnight. a sense of humor and a team-first mindset help.key responsibilitieskeep a pulse on the outside narrative. monitor news, social platforms (linkedin, x), podcasts, newsletters, and analyst and influencer commentary on our ceo, salesforce, our competitors, and the ai conversation. know what’s gaining traction, who is amplifying it, and what it means.keep our ceo’s message consistent. maintain a living bank of messaging, language, and approved stories so positioning doesn’t drift and every appearance builds on the last.ground everything in what’s been said. use transcripts, coverage, and past remarks to keep content accurate and avoid contradicting ourselves.flag what matters, fast. give our team timely, concise reads on emerging narratives, risks, and openings, including a short daily or weekly narrative brief. recommend whether and how we should engage.work cross-functionally. partner with product pr, the office of the ceo, government affairs, investor relations, and other teams to align on messaging and gather input.draft messaging. draft cue cards, talk tracks, scripts, and fireside chat questions and prep, from first draft to final, on tight and shifting deadlines.support media interviews. partner with media relations to prepare our ceo for press, podcast, and broadcast interviews: research the outlet and interviewer, and build key messages and q&a. afterward, flag takeaways and follow-ups, help with fact-checking, and capture strong soundbites for the messaging bank.helps own our ceo’s linkedin presence. write and publish posts in his voice, run the content calendar, and tie every post to the moments and narrative priorities that matter most. track performance and use it to sharpen what we post next.required skills / experience8+ years in executive communications, speechwriting, corporate communications, journalism, or a similar field. experience writing for a ceo or other senior spokesperson strongly preferred.exceptional writing and editing. a portfolio of speeches, talk tracks, op-eds, or executive messaging that is concise, compelling, and clearly in someone else’s voice.executive social media expertise. proven experience running linkedin for a senior leader: writing posts that sound like the person, planning a content calendar, and using engagement data to improve results.strong news and narrative judgment. a habit of reading the news and social conversation closely, spotting what’s gaining traction, and judging what matters, what doesn’t, and when to act. experience with media monitoring or social listening tools is a plus.fluency in the ai and enterprise technology landscape, or the curiosity to get there fast.high judgment and discretion. able to handle sensitive topics and confidential information with care.unleash your potentialwhen you join salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our ai agents accelerate your impact so you can do your position summary  position title: public relations specialist  department: integrated marketing  reports to: integrated marketing director  about the organization: the american association of critical-care nurses (aacn) is the largest specialty nursing organization in the world, representing the interests of more than 550,000 nurses who are charged with caring for acutely and critically ill patients. aacn is dedicated to creating a healthcare system driven by the needs of patients and families where acute and critical care nurses make their optimal contribution. visit us online at http://www.aacn.org .  aacn is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination against or harassment of any person employed by or seeking employment with aacn on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, sex and gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or related medical conditions, gender identity, gender expression, and sexual orientation), ancestry, national origin, age (40 or older), disability (mental and physical), military or veteran status, marital status, medical condition, or genetic information and any other basis protected by federal, state or local law or ordinance or regulation.  application instructions: interested individuals can visit our careers page and apply for the public relations specialist role. any questions can be directed to: jobs@aacn.org . this position is remote. some travel may be required. position purpose: the public relations specialist is responsible for independently evaluating, developing, and managing public relations, media relations, and external communications initiatives that support aacn’s strategic priorities, advocacy efforts, products, programs, and member engagement objectives.this role serves as a subject matter expert within the integrated marketing function, applying specialized knowledge in public relations, media relations, storytelling, messaging, and reputation management to evaluate communication needs, develop recommendations, and determine appropriate communication approaches and tactics aligned with organizational priorities.the public relations strategist partners with the integrated marketing director, organizational leaders, marketing teams, product owners, and external partners to identify communication opportunities, develop effective approaches, and deliver impactful communications that strengthen aacn’s visibility, reputation, and connection with key audiences.the role exercises independent judgment and discretion in managing complex communication assignments, evaluating opportunities and risks, determining appropriate communication approaches, and advising stakeholders on public relations activities. the position operates within established organizational strategy while independently determining methods, tactics, and execution approaches to achieve communication objectives.main accountabilities & results develops and executes public relations and media relations initiatives aligned with organizational priorities and communication strategies established by integrated marketing leadership. partners with the integrated marketing director and key stakeholders to translate organizational priorities into communication plans, messaging recommendations, media opportunities, and storytelling approaches.  provides subject matter expertise and recommendations regarding public relations opportunities, media engagement, audience considerations, messaging strategies, and communication tactics.  collaborates with business partners, product owners, marketing strategists, clinical leaders, and subject matter experts to identify opportunities to amplify organizational initiatives, programs, products, and thought leadership.  maintains a strong understanding of aacn’s mission, strategic priorities, governance structure, advocacy initiatives, healthcare environment, and industry trends to inform effective communication recommendations and execution.  evaluates and manages assigned media relations activities, including identifying opportunities, determining appropriate outreach and engagement approaches, responding to media inquiries, and developing relationships with journalists, media outlets, and external partners. develops and oversees communication materials, including press releases, media advisories, key messages, executive talking points, briefing documents, faqs, and other public relations resources, ensuring they reflect appropriate messaging, audience considerations, and organizational priorities.  builds and maintains relationships with media contacts and external partners to support aacn’s visibility, reputation, and thought leadership objectives.  monitors media coverage, industry trends, public conversations, and emerging issues to identify opportunities, assess communication needs, and provide recommendations to support organizational decision-making.  analyzes public relations outcomes, including media coverage, audience engagement, visibility, and other performance indicators, to assess effectiveness, identify opportunities and risks, and recommend adjustments to communication approaches.  maintains relationships with external public relations partners, vendors, and communication resources to support effective execution of initiatives.  partners with organizational leaders to support high-visibility communications that support executive leadership, crisis response, advocacy efforts, and organizational priorities. advises aacn leadership, including the president, president-elect, and board of directors, on media engagement by evaluating communication needs, recommending messaging and interview approaches, and developing briefing materials, talking points, and other communications aligned with established organizational priorities and messaging direction.  supports onboarding and communications planning for incoming presidents and presidents-elect by managing communication timelines, preparing messaging materials, coordinating media considerations, and ensuring communication needs are addressed.  partners with the director of integrated marketing and senior leaders to address media inquiries, emerging issues, and public-facing communication needs by providing recommendations, developing appropriate communications materials, and supporting implementation.  provides communications expertise for crisis and advocacy matters by assessing communication needs, evaluating risks, recommending approaches and priorities, developing materials, and independently managing assigned workstreams within established organizational direction.  collaborates across marketing and organizational teams to ensure communications are audience-focused and aligned with organizational priorities, providing public relations expertise and recommending tactics and approaches for crisis, advocacy, and high-priority communications. partners with the social media team to monitor conversations, audience sentiment, emerging issues, and relevant discussions, using insights to provide recommendations and inform communication approaches and opportunities for proactive engagement.  collaborates with marketing leaders and channel specialists to provide public relations expertise, recommend communication tactics, and support timelines and channel execution for crisis, advocacy, and high-priority organizational communications.  builds and maintains strong working relationships with internal stakeholders, external partners, and media contacts to support effective communication execution, collaboration, and organizational objectives.  upholds the organization’s talent philosophy and values.  performs other duties as assigned.  skills required :  demonstrated experience independently managing and executing public relations, media relations, and communications initiatives that support organizational priorities and established communication strategies.  advanced understanding of media relations practices, including media outreach, relationship management, story development, press materials, interview coordination, and media engagement processes.  exceptional writing and editing skills with demonstrated experience developing high-quality communications materials, including press releases, executive communications, talking points, faqs, media advisories, and other public-facing content.  ability to translate organizational priorities, products, advocacy initiatives, and clinical topics into compelling stories and communications materials that effectively engage target audiences.  strong understanding of integrated marketing and communications principles, including how public relations supports broader campaigns, organizational initiatives, and audience engagement efforts.  experience supporting crisis, issues management, and advocacy communications by coordinating messaging, developing communication materials, and executing approved communication plans across multiple channels.  strong collaboration and relationship-building skills with the ability to effectively partner with executives, volunteer leaders, media contacts, business partners, and cross-functional teams to support communication objectives.  experience using media monitoring, social listening, analytics, and audience insights to evaluate communication effectiveness, identify opportunities, and provide recommendations to improve engagement.  strong project management, organizational, and prioritization skills with the ability to independently manage multiple communication initiatives, coordinate deadlines, and ensure timely execution.  excellent judgment, discretion, communication, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage sensitive, high-visibility communications, evaluate situations, and determine appropriate next steps within established organizational priorities.  education and/or experience:  bachelor's degree in public relations, communications, journalism, marketing, english, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.  minimum 7 years of progressive experience in public relations, media relations, corporate communications, or a related field, with demonstrated ability to independently manage complex communications initiatives and deliver high-quality results with limited supervision.  demonstrated experience developing and managing public relations and communications strategies that support organizational priorities, brand awareness, stakeholder engagement, and business objectives, with the ability to independently assess communication needs and recommend appropriate approaches.  experience managing media relationships and evaluating media opportunities, including developing executive communications, messaging, talking points, briefing materials, and other communications aligned with organizational priorities.  experience managing crisis communications, advocacy communications, or issues management by assessing communication needs and risks, recommending messaging and communication approaches, and managing initiatives within established organizational direction.  experience exercising independent judgment in managing complex communications initiatives, prioritizing competing demands, advising cross-functional stakeholders, and evaluating communication effectiveness through media monitoring, audience insights, engagement metrics, and other measurement tools. physical requirementsin addition to the responsibilities outlined in the job description, the following requirements represent the essential functions of this job, which must be met by an individual to perform successfully. reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions. upon request, the organization will engage in an interactive process to identify and implement reasonable accommodations.this position involves frequent communication and collaboration with internal stakeholders, external partners, media contacts, and organizational leaders through virtual, in-person, and written communication channels. the role requires regular use of standard office equipment, including computer systems, and prolonged periods of desk work involving writing, research, communication planning, analysis, and content development. occasional travel may be required.the position requires the ability to evaluate information, analyze complex communication needs, exercise sound judgment, and determine appropriate approaches within established organizational priorities. the individual must demonstrate strong mental focus and attention to detail while managing multiple projects, competing priorities, sensitive communications, and evolving organizational needs.this role requires the ability to interpret and synthesize information, develop communication materials, provide recommendations, and collaborate effectively with cross-functional stakeholders. the individual must be able to work independently with limited supervision, prioritize assignments, resolve issues, and apply professional judgment to support organizational objectives and communication outcomes.total compensationthe target pay range for this role is $101,223 - $126,529 * we offer a 37.5-hour workweek with 3 different schedule options. in addition to the salary range listed, we offer a wealth of benefits to make working at aacn even more rewarding. benefits include generous paid time off, low-cost health plans for medical and mental health services, dental, and vision, company-paid life and short-term disability insurance, a variety of other benefits, and a retirement savings program with employer matching and additional company contribution. aacn is committed to a people-centered culture of workplace excellence and belonging, and offers various alternative and flexible work arrangements to support work/life balance for our team members.

deceptively simple questions:what are we actually trying to solve?who are we trying to move?what do we know about them that matters?what choice are we making because of it?how should that choice influence the work?and how will we know if it worked?that means you will:lead research and discovery across consumers, culture, categories and competitive environments.turn data, research and observations into insights people can actually use.define audiences based on behaviors, motivations and opportunities, not just demographics.frame business and communications problems clearly before teams jump to solutions.develop strategic positioning, communications strategies, briefs and planning frameworks.partner closely with creative, media, analytics, digital and account teams to connect strategy to execution.help teams understand not only what we’re recommending, but why.facilitate workshops and working sessions that move teams toward decisions.present strategic thinking to clients clearly, confidently and without hiding behind marketing language.stay connected to the work after the strategy is approved.use performance data to understand what we’re learning, what it means and what we should do differently.help identify opportunities to deepen client relationships and solve bigger business problems.raise the quality of strategic thinking around you.how we think about strategywe don’t believe strategy is a department people visit at the beginning of a project.strategy should create the connective tissue between the work.business → audience → insight → strategy → creative → media → performance → learningthe senior strategist helps make sure those things don’t become separate conversations.sometimes that means leading.sometimes it means challenging.sometimes it means simplifying.and sometimes it means being the person in the room willing to say, “i don’t think we’ve answered the real question yet.”what good looks likeyou create clarity where there wasn’t any.you can walk into a pile of research, analytics, client input, competitive activity and internal opinions and find the thing that actually matters.you make choices.you understand that a strategy that tries to accommodate everything isn’t a strategy.you connect dots.you can move comfortably between audience insights, creative ideas, media behavior and business performance without pretending to be the specialist in every discipline.you communicate simply.you can explain sophisticated thinking without making it sound sophisticated.you have a point of view.you aren’t afraid to challenge an assumption, but you know the difference between having an opinion and having an argument.you are accountable.you don’t throw a strategy over the wall and move on. you want to know what happened and what we learned.and you make the people around you better.what we’re looking forwe’re less interested in checking boxes than finding the right kind of thinker.but you’ll probably have:5-7+ years of experience in brand, communications, advertising or integrated marketing strategy.experience developing insights, briefs and strategic recommendations.strong research and analytical instincts — both quantitative and qualitative.the ability to synthesize large amounts of information quickly.experience working across creative, media, digital and analytics teams.confidence presenting and facilitating conversations with senior clients.strong writing and storytelling skills.comfort working with imperfect information and figuring out what needs to be known next.a healthy curiosity about people, businesses, culture, technology and why things work.experience mentoring or developing less-experienced strategists.*agency experience is valuable. intellectual curiosity is mandatory.the standardthe best strategic work should make the next decision easier. it should be clear enough that people understand it. connected enough that people know what it means for their work. and accountable enough that we can eventually determine whether we were right.a good senior strategist doesn’t just bring information into the room. they help the room decide what to do with it.note: salary range listed is an estimate, salary will also be based on experience

tools to both generate ideas, get stakeholders to see where an idea is headed, and to scale designexceptional craftpreferred qualificationscuriosity, ambition, and a distinct point of view on design, with strong typography skills and an appreciation for creative process, technology, and design engineering.are persuasive and humble in explaining your work, process, and decisionshave excellent partnering with cross-functional teams.creative coding or creative technologist background is a nice to havein-office expectationsoffice-assigned stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. this expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. for example, stripes in stripe delivery center roles in mexico city, mexico, bengaluru, india, and dublin, ireland work 100% from the office. also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. this approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.pay and benefitsthe annual us base salary range for this role is $175,200 - $262,800. for sales roles, the range provided is the role’s on target earnings ("ote") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. this salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the us may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.we look forward to hearing from you.at stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. you're encouraged to turns. at stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. join us.apply nowplease find our california applicant personal information who we areserval is an ai-native automation platform transforming how enterprises operate. we build intelligent agents that understand real-world workflows and execute them end-to-end — replacing manual processes and rigid legacy systems with adaptive, learning software. founded in early 2024, serval is already trusted by companies like fox, notion, perplexity, vercel, and brex to automate high-volume, high-friction operational work across their organizations.at the core of serval is an agentic ai platform that turns natural language into production-grade workflows. our agents don’t just respond to requests — they reason, take action across systems, and continuously improve with usage. what began with operational use cases has quickly evolved into a horizontal ai automation layer used across it, hr, finance, security, legal, and engineering.our mission is to eliminate repetitive, manual work across the enterprise and give teams leverage through intelligent automation. long term, we’re building the universal ai operations layer — a system of agents that sits across business functions and runs the workflows that keep modern companies moving.we’re backed by leading investors including sequoia capital, redpoint ventures, meritech, first round, general catalyst, elad gil, and others.role overviewas a senior designer, you'll guide the visual voice of serval, defining how an ai-native automation platform shows up in the world. you'll concept and execute creative work across every touchpoint: campaigns, web, product marketing, social, motion, print, merch, and events. you'll evolve our brand system and translate the technical depth of what we build into design that's distinctive, considered, and impossible to ignore.you'll jump fluidly between mediums, owning projects end-to-end from concept to launch with high creative autonomy. you'll partner closely with marketing, product, engineering, and leadership to define how serval shows up, and you'll set as important as the results we achieve. we provide professional excellence with joy and celebration to all those we serve. the needfor over 25 years, ijm has pioneered the work to protect vulnerable people from violence. 9 out of 9 times in the last decade, ijm’s justice system strengthening projects have reduced slavery and violence between 50 and 85% for very large populations of people in maintain clear review and approval pathways for factual accuracy, legal considerations, program strategy, calls to action, and safeguarding; build trusted, service-oriented partnerships across global marketing, global program, regional teams, and field offices; measure effectiveness and build learningdefine a measurement framework for programmatic marketing, including reach, comprehension, message uptake, sentiment, engagement, and appropriate behavioral or influence proxies; partner with program teams to connect communication indicators to program-owned outcome measures; establish baselines priorities, investment, and team structure needed to prove and scale the capability; recruit/develop a high-performing team as the function grows, fostering a culture of rigor, humility, and service; bring current best practices in behavior change, advocacy communication, audience research, and measurement; contribute as a strategic and collaborative member of the global marketing leadership team; and participation in ijm’s community of spiritual formation. qualifications: bachelor’s degree in research/behavioral sciences/market research, communications, international development, public development communication, or a related discipline, including at least four years in a leadership role; demonstrated success designing and delivering behavior-change or influence communication that contributed to measurable, documented results; experience working in or alongside international, multicultural, and field-based program contexts, with strong judgment regarding safeguarding all relevant stakeholders; demonstrated ability to build a new capability, operating model, or cross-functional practice in a complex organization; deep expertise in social and behavior change communication and strong working knowledge of advocacy or public-affairs communication; expertise in formative research, audience segmentation, behavioral and social-norms approaches, message creative execution; experience with media and social-listening approaches, narrative risk assessment, and rapid communication response; and excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the
