covista is america's largest healthcare educator, serving more than 97,000 students and supported by a community of 385,000 alumni across five accredited institutions. through personalized, tech-enabled education powered by 10,000 faculty and colleagues, covista expands access to healthcare careers and addresses the u.s. healthcare workforce shortage at scale. covista is the parent company of american university of the caribbean school of medicine, chamberlain university, ross university school of medicine, ross university school of veterinary medicine and walden university.our colleagues come from a wide range of backgrounds, business, academia, healthcare, government and nonprofits, and are part of a culture where doing exceptional work and making a meaningful difference for students and society aren't separate goals—they're one and the same. this means creating an environment where colleagues can develop new skills, build careers that match their ambitions and see the tangible impact of their work on healthcare education and workforce development. colleagues who deliver results and embrace new tools to work smarter are valued for their contributions. but what makes working at covista distinctive is our impact. our faculty and colleagues don't just support healthcare education—they shape it. this isn't abstract purpose work. it's solving real problems for real people in real communities while advancing careers.we operate on a hybrid schedule with four in-office days per week (monday–thursday). this approach enhances creativity, innovation, communication, and relationship-building, fostering a dynamic and collaborative work environment. job descriptionyou'll be the steady hand behind how covista's first team (our executive leadership) shows up publicly—building and executing the executive communications that shape how our ceo and other first team leaders are seen and heard. reporting directly to the director of corporate communications, you'll own the day-to-day mechanics of executive positioning: keeping every workstream on track, every voice consistent and every piece of content polished and on time.this role is built for someone who thrives on precision and process as much as prose. you'll manage multiple executives' content calendars and priorities simultaneously, translate a leader's point of view into a linkedin post that actually performs, and make sure everything moves forward on schedule.the exposure is broad and the work is high visibility. you'll support the first team on the moments that define their public presence—thought leadership, linkedin engagement, speaking engagements and the steady drumbeat of content that builds their authority over time.key responsibilities:executive communicationsdraft speeches, talking points, bylined articles and presentations tailored to each first team member's voice and priorities. own day-to-day execution of executive social media, with a particular focus on linkedin—writing, scheduling, monitoring engagement and identifying trends and moments to capitalize on. build and maintain messaging frameworks and content calendars across multiple executives and audiences. support media and speaking engagement prep, including briefing materials and q&as. track and manage multiple concurrent executive workstreams, ensuring deadlines, approvals and details don't fall through the cracks. use ai and technology to sharpen your work and move faster. performs other duties as assigned. complies with all policies and standards. who thrives hereyou're exceptionally organized—the person who keeps five executives' priorities straight without breaking a sweat, and who never lets a detail slip. you've supported senior leaders directly before and understand the pace, discretion and precision that comes with it. you write well across voices and formats, and you have a strong feel for what makes content land on linkedin—not just what to post, but when, how, and why it'll resonate. you're proactive, low-ego, and comfortable being the person behind the scenes making an executive look good.qualificationsbachelor's degree in communications, marketing, journalism or a related field required. 7+ years of experience directly supporting c-suite or senior executive leaders in a communications capacity—in-house, agency or both. proven organizational rigor: experience managing multiple executives' content pipelines, calendars and priorities at once. exceptional writing: able to write convincingly in multiple executive voices and adapt across formats. social media fluency: hands-on experience managing executive linkedin presence and driving measurable engagement. discretion and judgment: comfortable handling sensitive information and high-stakes situations with maturity. comfort with ai tools: actively uses ai to produce better work, faster. preferred backgroundexperience in higher education, healthcare, publicly traded companies or regulated industries is a plus. you're as comfortable in a strategic conversation as you are executing the details flawlessly. you build trust easily—with internal teams, external partners, and media contacts alike. #cvsaadditional informationin support of the pay transparency laws enacted across the country, the expected salary range for this position is between $80,336.75 and detail.desc: public relations manager reports to senior vice president of news and public relations androvett is seeking an experienced public relations manager who can take ownership of client relationships, provide thoughtful strategic counsel and independently move communications programs forward. we're looking for a pr professional who brings strong news judgment, initiative and the confidence to lead. someone who understands what clients are trying to accomplish, identifies opportunities to advance their goals and turns thoughtful recommendations into results. this position offers meaningful responsibility for client accounts, from developing strategy and counseling clients to media relations, content development and day-to-day execution. our clients operate in sophisticated, often reputation-sensitive environments, requiring sound judgment, responsiveness and consistently excellent work. the right person will be comfortable making decisions and moving work forward independently while contributing to a collaborative team that values accountability, professionalism and high-quality work. responsibilities client leadership and strategic counsel serve as a day-to-day client contact and trusted advisor, taking ownership of client relationships, communications programs and results. lead client meetings, provide strategic counsel, manage expectations and ensure work remains on time and within scope. anticipate client needs, recognize potential challenges and proactively recommend solutions. develop and implement pr strategies aligned with client business objectives, bringing thoughtful recommendations and a clear point of view. exercise independent judgment, recognize communications opportunities and reputational risks, and respectfully challenge assumptions when a different approach would better serve the client. media relations and opportunity development proactively identify and develop earned media, thought leadership and other communications opportunities that advance client objectives, visibility and reputation. develop and pitch compelling story ideas to local, regional and national media, recognizing strong news angles and understanding the needs of journalists. build and maintain productive relationships with reporters, editors, producers and other media professionals. prepare and position clients for media interviews and other public-facing opportunities. monitor relevant news, industry developments and emerging issues to identify timely opportunities for clients. writing, content and execution translate complex legal, business and industry topics into clear, accurate and compelling communications for a variety of audiences, collaborating with marketing, digital and creative colleagues on integrated communications strategies. write, edit and oversee news releases, authored commentaries, blog posts, social media content, white papers, professional biographies, talking points, video content and other communications materials. collaborate with marketing, digital and creative colleagues to develop website content, social media programs and integrated communications strategies. measure communications results, evaluate effectiveness and recommend adjustments or next steps. use ai-enabled research, writing and productivity tools responsibly, exercising appropriate fact-checking, editorial oversight and confidentiality. account and project management independently manage multiple client accounts, projects, deadlines and priorities, taking initiative to resolve obstacles and move work forward without constant direction. respond effectively to changing priorities and deadline-sensitive situations, balancing urgency with sound judgment and recognizing when review or escalation is necessary. provide direction, feedback and support to junior team members while remaining accountable for the quality and timely completion of work. collaborate across the agency, drawing on colleagues' expertise to develop effective client solutions. identify opportunities to strengthen existing client relationships and increase the value of androvett's services. experience required bachelor's degree in journalism, communications or a related field. a minimum of five years of relevant professional experience in public relations, communications, journalism or related work. approximately 5–8 years of experience is preferred for this position. experience in one or more of the following: news reporting, producing or editing agency account service in-house public relations or communications management experience working with b2b clients or organizations on complex communications topics. demonstrated client service and account management experience, including responsibility for advancing client programs and managing deliverables. strong media relations, writing, editing and strategic communications capabilities. experience preferred public relations agency experience, particularly managing multiple client accounts. professional-services experience, particularly with law firms, attorneys or organizations in the legal, public affairs, healthcare or energy sectors. crisis communications, issues management, litigation communications or reputation management experience. experience integrating traditional media relations with digital content, social media and broader marketing initiatives. skills that will make you stand out a demonstrated record of developing successful pr opportunities and delivering measurable results for clients. experience serving as a lead advisor on complex, sensitive or high-profile communications matters. established relationships with journalists and a strong understanding of today's media environment. knowledge of emerging communications, media and digital trends and the ability to apply them practically. familiarity with photo and video-editing tools and other content development capabilities. we offer salary commensurate with experience medical, dental and vision benefits paid time off and company holidays 401(k) program free parking a hybrid work schedule, with in-office collaboration on tuesdays and wednesdays and remote work on mondays, thursdays and fridays about androvett androvett is a full-service marketing firm offering public relations, advertising, marketing, brand strategy, and web and digital solutions that achieve client business goals. founded in 1995 with a focus on connecting lawyers, law firms and their clients with the media, androvett today serves a range of industries from offices in dallas, houston, austin and san antonio. our work is grounded in sound judgment, strong relationships, thoughtful strategy and excellent execution. we value people who take responsibility for their work, communicate professionally, collaborate effectively and continually look for ways to improve. our core values reflect those commitments: earn trust, aim for excellence, demonstrate ownership, show respect and commit to learning. we're looking for a pr manager who shares those values and is ready to take meaningful responsibility for helping our clients succeed.

$95k.our office has a hybrid work model: in office 3 days a week (tues-thurs), remote 2 days a week.dkc provides equal employment opportunities to applicants and employees without regard for factors beneath even the most unruly situations — whether it's a global crisis, an emerging technology, or a sweeping organizational change—lies a simple human need. that need could be for trust, connection, strategy and media engagement for microsoft's business, helping protect and strengthen brand reputation by translating complex issues into clear, credible narratives for key audiences.this role involves managing day-to-day client needs, driving pr campaigns, and fostering strong media and influencer relationships. ideal candidates are proactive communicators with strong analytical writing, relationship-management skills, and a passion for helping organizations communicate clearly in moments that matter. this role may manage direct reports.responsibilitiesmanage company news announcements and media cycles across corporate issues, helping to coordinate responses and drive execution in fast-paced environments. build and maintain relationships with reporters, industry influencers, and content creators, identifying opportunities to place stories and interviews to strengthen client visibility. serve as day-to-day counsel for clients and internal stakeholders, providing informed recommendations, managing expectations, flagging risks early and keeping workstreams aligned and on schedule. lead planning sessions and brainstorms, helping identify creative storytelling opportunities and new approaches to audience engagement. draft and develop a wide range of communications materials, including pitches, media materials like faqs, executive briefing documents, reactive statements, and coverage reports. monitor and analyze media, social, industry and competitive conversations to identify emerging reputational risks and opportunities; translate findings into actionable recommendations that protect and strengthen brand trust. support integrated earned, owned, social, and influencer campaigns that advance business objectives by coordinating deliverables and tracking performance coordinate cross-functional efforts across multiple client, agency, and partner teams to gather information, align messaging, and support program execution. may manage career development and performance of direct reports, managing up to senior staff on important issues, and client/team satisfaction while holding the team accountable to demonstrating agency values other duties as assigned requirements4+ years of experience in integrated communications or pr, preferably in an agency setting and/or within an applicable industry; 1+ years of management experience preferred minimum of 3 years of experience in strategic communications, corporate image, and/or issues management. proficiency with microsoft office suite (particularly outlook, word, sharepoint, powerpoint and excel) and experience using ai tools like copilot. preferred qualificationsexperience working with clients in the technology or science industry. demonstrated customer service orientation and ability to establish a consulting relationship with clients. high level of initiative; take accountability for role on projects. experience engaging with reporters and pitching stories; having established media and/or creator influencer relationships is a plus. demonstrated creative and strategic mindset, and ability to synthesize complex information and translate it into clear, compelling content for a variety of audiences. ability to analyze the news and social media environment, and provide strategic recommendations based on business and industry knowledge. exceptional attention to detail and strong editorial judgment, including proficiency in ap style and ability to edit for accuracy, clarity and consistency. desire to work in a fast-paced team environment (frequent tight deadlines, shifting priorities, multitasking, etc.); job pressure may exist from requirement of handling multiple tasks. ability to read, write, and speak english and experience working with colleagues or clients across multiple locations. may need to work more than 40 hours per week on occasion. compensationthe base annual salary range for this role, applicable about poshwe are all social creatures, but the dominant “social” companies today have evolved into digital loneliness machines, driving isolation, anxiety, and mental health challenges around the world.human connection is lost. posh is a beacon guiding us back.posh enables anyone to build an irl community based on shared interests, while connecting consumers with the communities of people just like them. founded by event organizers who were frustrated with the growing loneliness epidemic and the tools available to build their own event brand, we’ve built the ultimate platform for launching, monetizing, and finding irl communities of people just like you. in just 6 years, posh has grown to a team of 70, expanded to 10m+ users, secured $70m in venture funding, and facilitated over $400m in transactions.brand is the only moat that compounds without code. posh isn't a product people quietly use — it's an aesthetic, a lifestyle, a culture people identify with. as we scale past 10m users and the consumer + organizer surface area expands, the way posh looks, sounds, and feels is what will separate us from being one of many event platforms and being the cultural home of irl community.as brand designer, you'll own the visual and creative identity of posh end-to-end — defining what the brand looks like across every surface, leading the in-house and agency talent that brings it to life, and setting the bar that every campaign, asset, and touchpoint is held to. you'll personally create where it matters most and orchestrate where it scales, holding the line on a brand that earns a place in people's lives, not just their feeds.your work will span across 2 core areasbrand & culture: owning brand identity, campaigns, content, merchandise, partnerships, event activations, and the storytelling that lives on tiktok, instagram, and irl — the work that makes posh feel like a movement, not a marketplace.gtm creative system: setting and defending the creative bar across every channel posh shows up in — brand marketing, product marketing, performance creative, sales & success enablement, community, and in-product moments — so the brand is unmistakably cohesive whether a user encounters us in an ad, a user flow, or a pitch deck.this role reports to the ceo and partners directly with product and gtm leadership to ensure brand cohesion at every possible touchpoint.this is an in-person position at our soho nyc office, 5 days a week.what you'll own & achievedefine what posh looks like in 2027. evolve our visual identity, design language, and creative principles for the next chapter of the brand — and codify them clearly enough that every team and outside partner can build to the same bar.create the work yourself when it matters. roughly half of what ships should come from your own hands — the hero campaigns, social assets, merch drops, and company moments that need a singular point of view. you're a maker first, a director second.build the agency and contractor stack that scales the other half. source, brief, and manage the freelancers, studios, photographers, and motion artists who let posh punch above its in-house weight. own the quality bar across every external partner.make the brand undeniably cohesive across every surface. stand up the systems, templates, and review rituals that ensure brand, product marketing, performance creative, sales decks, community assets, and in-product moments all feel like one company.set the creative bar for product marketing and performance. partner with growth and product marketing to make posh's paid, lifecycle, and product launch creative as cohesive and engaging as possible.be the brand's loudest internal advocate. push back when work doesn't meet the bar, regardless of who shipped it. run critiques, mentor non-designers on taste, and make creative excellence a company-wide standard rather than a marketing-team concern.stay ahead of culture, not behind it. live inside the music, nightlife, fashion, and creator worlds that posh exists at the intersection of. bring trends, references, and collaborations into our work at every chance.leverage ai as a creative force-multiplier. bring image, video, and ideation tooling into your daily workflow — using ai to compress turnaround on iterations, expand creative range, and ship at a velocity that small in-house teams traditionally can't.who you are5+ years in design, art direction, or creative rolesa portfolio that speaks for itself: campaign work, brand systems, merch, motion, social content, partnerships. we want to see creative you’ve made with your own hands and at-scale systems you led others through.equally fluent in making and directing. you can sit in figma or after effects and ship the work yourself, and you can brief an agency or a freelance motion artist and get back something that meets your bar.a real point of view on the music, nightlife, events, and irl culture worlds. you don't just read about them — you live in them and have the relationships, references, and instincts to prove it.mastery of adobe creative suite, figma, and modern motion tools. generative ai (image, video, and ideation) is a daily part of your workflow, not an experiment.sharp written and verbal communication. you can write a brief, defend a creative decision in a leadership review, and align a non-designer stakeholder on why something needs to ship differently.a bias toward urgency and high output. you ship a high volume of work without compromising the bar; you know when to perfect and when to release.high eq. you can give and receive direct creative feedback, manage external partners with care, and build trust with cross-functional teams who don't always speak creative.nice to havepast experience as the in-house creative leader at a consumer brand at series b–d scale that punched well above its size on brand (liquid death, poppi, olipop, partiful, cash app, ramp, on, aimé leon dore, or outside the 9-to-5.direct experience working with musicians, artists, venues, or labels on creative partnerships.a deep personal connection to irl events, nightlife, or the kinds of communities posh communications strategistjob description department:                          communicationsemployment type:                regular full-timesupervisory:                         nosalary schedule:                 l2location:                            el pasobu/nbu:                              bargaining unit organization overviewthe american civil liberties union of texas is one of the leading civil rights organizations in the lone star state. we work in courts, legislatures, and communities to protect and extend the civil rights for texans throughout the state. the aclu of texas is both a nonprofit and nonpartisan organization. the aclu of texas operates professional offices in houston, austin, dallas, el paso, and brownsville, texas.department overviewthe communications department educates and activates texans to work with the aclu of texas for strategic change in the areas of criminal legal reform, democracy and voting rights, border and immigrants' rights, free speech and pluralism, lgbtqia+ equality, and reproductive freedom across the state. role overviewthe aclu of texas seeks a communications strategist to design communications efforts that protect and advance the rights of all texans. this person plays a critical role in educating the public, building political power, and achieving advocacy wins across two or more issue areas of the aclu of texas, including voting rights, lgbtqia+ rights, immigrants’ rights, smart justice, and reproductive freedom. we’re looking for someone who thrives in the energy and intensity of advocacy work and knows how to craft messaging and tactics that move issues forward. ideal candidates will have excellent written and verbal communication skills, manage time and projects well, be willing to take creative risks, pay close attention to detail, and demonstrate a commitment to civil rights and racial equity.the communications strategist reports to the strategic communications manager and works closely with colleagues within the department and across the organization. responsibilities campaign development: proposes and designs communications plans for advocacy campaigns and rapid response moments that advance integrated advocacy goals related to two or more issue areas; implements plans across paid, earned, shared, and owned media in coordination with colleagues and vendors; brings a strategic communications lens to issue-area meetings across teams and in coalition.content production: supports digital and press experts in drafting messaging, press releases, blogs, op-eds, social posts, reports, fact sheets, and other communications materials for advocacy efforts; uses analytics to evolve content.general: develops relationships with colleagues across the aclu network to collaborate on campaigns and share resources; supports the department with other duties as assigned.competencieswritten and verbal communication: contributes to the development of original messaging and builds out talking points. quickly produces high-quality written products for different media channels and audiences. able to communicate with internal and external stakeholders clearly and with empathy.strategic mindset: expands knowledge of how to anticipate future opportunities and consequences. learns from past experience. proposes original strategies and plans for two issue areas that are inclusive, prudent, and actionable. triages complex situations and encourages stakeholder buy-in.project management: able to develop task concepts and break down activities into manageable pieces that can be individually and collaboratively executed with internal colleagues and external vendors. manages vendors for small-sized contracts. tracks progress using project management tools. completes deliverables on schedule.teamwork: brings a positive, problem-solving attitude to relationships with colleagues and partners. relates well with people of different backgrounds and responsibilities. demonstrates personal integrity, admits mistakes, and fosters trust.decision-making: “owns” the work in the project area. makes smart decisions that reflect clear reasoning and awareness of impact. works with the appropriate level of supervision. knows when to ask questions or when to ask for help.qualificationsa bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, or related field; work experience and/or alternative educational preparation in the competencies listed above may be substituted for formal education.3+ years of experience in advocacy communications, preferably related to one or more of the following issues: criminal legal reform, democracy and voting rights, immigration, lgbtqia+ equality, and reproductive freedom.excellent writing and editing skills in a range of digital and press formats. proven record of published content and understanding of ap style. ability to communicate. persuasively to a wide variety of media, political, stakeholder, community, and influencer audiences.solid computer skills, including proficiency in word processing, spreadsheet, and communications tools.flexible schedule and ability to work non-traditional hours as needed. some travel required.demonstrated commitment to advancing the aclu of texas’ values, mission, and goals, with an understanding of structural racism and interpersonal bias.preferred qualifications:strong project management skills. ability to delegate and coordinate deliverables across teams in a fast-paced environment with shifting demands.strategic acumen in paid, earned, shared, and owned media channels.experience working in coalitions.fluency in spanish.compensationstarting salary is $70,000 - $76,000 year in alignment with the parameters of aclu of texas’ salary scale. excellent benefits include a generous paid time off policy; medical, dental and vision insurance; 401(k) plan with an employer match; life and long-term disability insurance, and compare plans, apply for financial help, and buy health insurance. as colorado’s official health insurance marketplace, we are the only place to apply for financial help to lower the monthly cost of premiums. customers can shop online; get help by phone or online chat from customer service center representatives; and access expert help from a statewide network of certified insurance brokers and community-based assisters. our mission is to increase access, affordability, and choice for individuals and small employers purchasing health insurance in colorado. for more information, visit connectforhealthco.composition summarythe senior communications strategist (policy & internal communications) reports to the senior communications manager and supports the development and execution of into clear, audience-focused communications that strengthen trust and engagement. they will also coordinate communications across teams and support high-volume initiatives such as the annual open enrollment period. they will be comfortable working in the rapidly evolving health policy landscape, and will ensure communications align with c4hco’s strategy, voice, and priorities.in addition to content development and execution, the senior communications strategist supports the senior communications manager to create the strategy for policy and internal communications, in alignment with c4hco’s priorities.when appropriate, the senior communications strategist may represent c4hco in public meetings or external, collaborative initiatives.position responsibilitiesdevelop and execute strategic policy and internal communications that align with organizational priorities and communications strategies. craft, review, and deploy written communications including policy memos, stakeholder emails, talking points, press releases, product announcements, faqs, and partner engagement materials.serve as a liaison to improve policy and internal communications, identify communication gaps, and resolve complex communication challenges in coordination with internal teams.contribute to integrated communications campaigns across email, web, social media, and partner networks.translate health policy information, organizational priorities, product updates, and enrollment information into clear, audience-specific messaging.participate in stakeholder meetings and represent c4hco in partner communications efforts to support coordinated messaging and engagement. contribute to rapid-response communications and issue management efforts, ensuring timely and accurate messaging. support open enrollment communications strategy, planning, and execution, including high-volume, time-sensitive tasks and coordination of messaging.ensure alignment between customer-facing and internal communication.identify opportunities to streamline communications processes and strengthen cross-functional coordination.support the senior communications manager in building and maintaining a disciplined, insight-driven communications function aligned with c4hco priorities.monitor engagement metrics and stakeholder feedback; provide insights and recommendations to refine communications strategies and improve reach, clarity, and impact.perform other duties as needed in support of departmental and organizational priorities.requirementscolorado resident.bachelor’s degree in communications, public policy, marketing, journalism, public relations, or a related field.3–5 years of experience in policy communications, public policy, public relations, or related field.strong writing and editing skills across multiple formats – policy memos, emails, web content, internal communications, and customer notices. ability to translate complex the director of media relations leads the atlantic council’s media outreach and communications strategy, and serves on the leadership of the broader engagement team. the director is responsible for bolstering the council’s media profile—advancing its mission by amplifying its expertise, events, and publications through earned us and international coverage. the director also coordinates external communications efforts and campaigns across the institution.the director reports to the atlantic council’s senior editorial director. the director works closely with the council’s digital, editorial, and event-production teams; executive office; and the atlantic council’s various programs and centers.this position is based at the council’s washington, dc headquarters. the director is expected in the office at least four days a week, and whenever the role requires.the atlantic council offers a competitive compensation package commensurate with experience and education, with offers from $140,000 to $180,000, and the position is bonus-eligible. applications submitted by november 1, 2026 will be prioritized for consideration.job responsibilitiesmedia relationsmanage the atlantic council’s media-relations operation, including full-time team members, partners, and vendors.build and manage relationships with reporters, producers, bookers, and editors at top-level us and international print, digital, and broadcast outlets.identify opportunities for and secure high-profile media coverage of atlantic council events and publications.lead rapid response to the media on breaking news developments worldwide, inserting the council’s expert views into the news cycle when they are most relevant.serve as the primary point of contact for crisis communications and rapid response.generate media partnerships that raise the visibility of council events and initiatives.coordinate efforts to secure media moderators and panelists.edit and place opinion columns in leading outlets.train staff on best practices for engaging with print, digital, and broadcast media.travel as needed to support the council’s global and flagship convenings.establish council experts as pre-eminent and visible sources of commentary and insight on international affairs.strategic communicationslead the atlantic council’s overall approach to external media as spokesperson, strategist, and advocate.help to build greater public awareness of the council, its influence, and the impact of its work, particularly in the press.develop a strategy to increase the atlantic council’s presence on non-traditional media platforms, including engagement with podcasts and digital media influencers.serve as a lead communications representative at the outset of major new atlantic council initiatives, defining a holistic communications framework including tactics and strategy.oversee long-term communications planning for the council’s programs and centers, working with each to define programmatic goals and a matching strategy.manage the council-wide communications calendar, including council and external global events, to raise the organization’s profile around key moments.develop the council’s paid media strategy in partnership with colleagues.lead and expand the council’s evolving portfolio of media partnerships.qualificationsrequiredbachelor’s degree in international affairs, communications, journalism, or a related field.7-10+ years of media relations, journalism, or strategic-communications experience, including at least three years managing staff.a robust network of active relationships with journalists at top-tier national and international outlets covering foreign policy, security, technology, and economics.experience designing and leading organization-wide communications plans and campaigns across multiple teams or programs.a track record of securing high-impact coverage, including broadcast bookings and op-ed placements.excellent writing and editing skills, with the ability to produce pitches, releases, and talking points on tight deadlines.working knowledge of international affairs and the washington policy landscape.proficiency with social media, digital marketing, and ai tools.proven judgment in crisis communications and in handling sensitive issues.ability to work outside standard hours when breaking news or other time-sensitive matters require it.preferredexperience at a major newsroom, government agency or congressional office, international organization, or policy institution.experience with media in europe, the middle east, asia, africa, or latin america.experience developing paid media strategies or managing media partnerships.proficiency in a second language.familiarity with media monitoring and database platforms such as cision, meltwater, or muck rack.how to applyto apply through the atlantic council careers page, submit a resume and cover letter. applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, with those submitted by november 1, 2026, prioritized for consideration.to produce quality work and to successfully achieve our mission, we recognize the need for our staff to maintain a healthy lifestyle and a work/life balance. our comprehensive benefits package helps to keep costs low for our staff and their families. benefits include, but are not limited to comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, 403(b) plan, fsa options, pet insurance, public service loan forgiveness eligibility, and wellness benefits.

who we areinternational justice mission (ijm) is the global leader in protecting vulnerable people from violence around the world. our team of over 1,200 professionals are at work worldwide in over 30 offices. together we are on a mission to rescue millions, protect half a billion, and make justice unstoppable.we are a global community that cares for one another. we believe that the way we work is as important as the results we achieve. we provide professional excellence with joy and celebration to all those we serve. the needfor over 25 years, ijm has pioneered the work to protect vulnerable people from violence. 9 out of 9 times in the last decade, ijm’s justice system strengthening projects have reduced slavery and violence between 50 and 85% for very large populations of people in poverty. as we grow to expand our impact to protect 500 million people from violence, we are seeking a director, programmatic marketing enablement to establish and lead the capability through which ijm’s global marketing function advances programmatic outcomes. working at the intersection of marketing, program delivery, advocacy, and justice-system influence, this leader will help program teams use strategic communication to influence the audiences, decisions, behaviors, and social norms that matter to their objectives.this position is hybrid (onsite tuesdays & thursdays) if located in the washington, dc area or remote for non-local candidates and reports to the vice president, global insights and growth. this role requires current authorization to work in the united states. visa sponsorship is not available for this position, now or in the future.responsibilities:build the programmatic marketing capabilitydefine the strategy, scope, service model, and standards for how global marketing supports program-owned behavior-change and influence objectives; assess existing work across ijm and build on field and program expertise rather than duplicating or displacing it; establish a disciplined process for intake, sensitivity assessment, prioritization, staffing, roles/responsibilities framework, and delivery of programmatic marketing work; this should be in conjunction with global marketing’s existing operations model; translate program objectives into marketing & communications strategypartner with global program, advocacy, and field leaders early to determine where strategic marketing can advance program-defined outcomes; translate those outcomes into focused communication strategies that define the priority audience, the desired change, the communication approach, and how effectiveness will be measured; use research and local insight to understand what may motivate or prevent the intended audience from changing its knowledge, attitudes, decisions, or behavior; develop audience-centered strategies that support behavior change, community influence, or decision-maker engagement, depending on the program objective; lead integrated campaign deliverylead initial pilot campaigns from strategy through execution in partnership with global marketing capability experts; develop integrated channel plans that reach priority audiences through the most effective mix of mass, digital, community, interpersonal, and partner-led communication; engage trusted messengers such as journalists, faith leaders, and community leaders to strengthen the reach and credibility of priority efforts; manage visibility and narrative risk by monitoring public response, addressing harmful or unintended narratives, and ensuring all public-facing communication follows program direction and approved sensitivity levels; protect program integrity and safeguardingensure all work reflects local context, protects survivors and staff, and complies with ijm safeguarding, legal, security, consent, and brand requirements; apply program-defined sensitivity and visibility classifications so confidential or protected work is never unintentionally amplified; maintain clear review and approval pathways for factual accuracy, legal considerations, program strategy, calls to action, and safeguarding; build trusted, service-oriented partnerships across global marketing, global program, regional teams, and field offices; measure effectiveness and build learningdefine a measurement framework for programmatic marketing, including reach, comprehension, message uptake, sentiment, engagement, and appropriate behavioral or influence proxies; partner with program teams to connect communication indicators to program-owned outcome measures; establish baselines and learning plans for priority efforts and use evidence to improve audience strategy, messaging, creative, channels, and partner selection; build and scale the functionestablish the roadmap, priorities, investment, and team structure needed to prove and scale the capability; recruit/develop a high-performing team as the function grows, fostering a culture of rigor, humility, and service; bring current best practices in behavior change, advocacy communication, audience research, and measurement; contribute as a strategic and collaborative member of the global marketing leadership team; and participation in ijm’s community of spiritual formation. qualifications: bachelor’s degree in research/behavioral sciences/market research, communications, international development, public affairs, marketing, or a related field; master’s degree preferred; at least nine years of relevant experience in social and behavior change communication, advocacy or public-affairs communication, development communication, or a related discipline, including at least four years in a leadership role; demonstrated success designing and delivering behavior-change or influence communication that contributed to measurable, documented results; experience working in or alongside international, multicultural, and field-based program contexts, with strong judgment regarding safeguarding all relevant stakeholders; demonstrated ability to build a new capability, operating model, or cross-functional practice in a complex organization; deep expertise in social and behavior change communication and strong working knowledge of advocacy or public-affairs communication; expertise in formative research, audience segmentation, behavioral and social-norms approaches, message development, integrated campaign design, and communication measurement; ability to translate complex program objectives into focused audience and communication strategies and to guide high-quality creative execution; experience with media and social-listening approaches, narrative risk assessment, and rapid communication response; and excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to work effectively from field-level briefs through executive-level decisions. critical qualities:eager commitment to ijm's core values: christian, professional and bridge-building; self-starter with strong initiative;  disciplined with priorities; strong interpersonal skills and self-awareness; exceptional verbal and written communication; flexible, collaborative and eager to support others; effective team player who fosters collaborative environment; and adept at creative problem solving. mature christian faith as defined by the apostles’ creed; builder’s mindset, strategic judgment, and the ability to turn ambiguity into a clear and practical path forward; high emotional intelligence and cultural humility, with a demonstrated ability to earn trust across functions, geographies, and levels of seniority; strong ethic of service and deep commitment to ijm’s mission, safeguarding principles, and organizational values; results-oriented, self-directed, organized, and able to operate with significant independence while collaborating closely with others; and servant leadership that consistently places mission, survivors, program partners, and team outcomes above personal agenda. application process: upload resume, cover letter & statement of faith* in one pdf document.what is a statement of faith? a statement of faith should describe your christian faith and how you see it as relevant to your involvement with ijm. the statement can either be incorporated into the cover letter or submitted as a separate document and should include, at a minimum, a description of your spiritual disciplines (prayer, study, etc.) and your current fellowship or place of worship. what does ijm have to offer?comprehensive medical/dental/vision benefits monthly commuter and parking benefits in the dc metro area retirement benefit options paid leave starting at 23 days 12 holidays (plus early release the day prior) daily, quarterly, and annual community spiritual formation robust staff care resources ijm holds strict safeguarding principles and a zero tolerance to violations of the safeguarding policy, protection against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment policy, and code of ethics. candidate selection is based on technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring criteria subject to assessing the candidate’s value congruence and thorough background, police clearance, and reference check processes.at ijm, we’re committed to building a diverse workforce through fair and equitable employment practices. ijm encourages people of any race, color, age, sex, marital status or political ideology to apply for employment. while we welcome everyone into this work, we truly believe that the work we are doing is god’s work, not our own, and practice spiritual disciplines together daily. that’s why we legally require under sec. 2000e-1 [section702] of title vii of the civil rights act of 1964 that all employees practice a mature orthodox christian faith, as defined by the apostles’ creed.ijm requires a background check, police clearance and thorough review of references with an employment offer and/or employment contract.

by:developing better, longer-lasting solutions that reflect the priorities of ordinary people;creating the space for decision-makers from across the political spectrum to lead on environmental issues on their own terms; andbuilding confidence, capability and credibility in places where environmental action has too often been framed as belonging to one side of politics.och’s model depends on local credibility. country teams know their audiences, politics, language and media environments best. the central team exists to strengthen that work, not to direct it. a small global team sets the mission and supports country teams on strategy, research, governance and fundraising.why this role matters nowthe media and information environment is changing fast. trust is fragmenting, audiences are harder to reach through traditional channels, and ai is reshaping how information is produced, discovered, summarised and repeated. generic content is losing value. the premium is moving towards trusted voices, credible data, distinctive insight and rapid relevance.that shift plays to och's strengths, but only if the network is built for where media is heading rather than where it has been. the successful candidate will help och partners build the infrastructure to build up credible voices, develop them, connect them to the right media and platforms, and ensure their stories and evidence travel across the network.purpose of the rolethe global director of strategic communications will build and lead och's central strategic communications and public-influence function. the role will define what good media engagement work looks like across the network, support countries to develop their own capacity, and create shared systems that allow learning, intelligence and media opportunities to travel quickly.the consistent priority is to amplify partners and credible local voices rather than to raise och's own profile. the postholder will have the authority, licence and resources to build the infrastructure needed to do that well.the role works across three levelspartner and spokesperson amplification. elevating credible conservative and centre-right voices already rooted in communities through the network's partners and ground game, led by local people and local stories.country entity communications. helping national entities develop their own public presence, earned-media capacity, spokesperson base and public-influence strategy, without taking ownership of their political positioning.och central communications. developing the strategy for och's own public profile where it is useful to the mission, while keeping the primary emphasis on the network and local voices.what success looks likeafter the first year, success would mean that och has a clear media engagement strategy, a small but effective central capability, shared standards and methods, a tested spokesperson-development process, priority-country plans, and a growing rapid-response model.after three years, success would mean that country teams have the tools, confidence, relationships and judgement to lead their own public-influence work; credible conservative and centre-right environmental voices are more visible in national debates across priority countries; and the centre has moved from doing the work to advising, coaching and strengthening it.key responsibilitiesbuild och's central strategic communications and public-influence capability, including shaping the team, external support and operating model required for the build phase.define what good media engagement work looks like across the network: the shared language, standards, frameworks and practical tools that country teams can adapt to their contexts.work directly with country teams in the early phase to develop their strategies, then move progressively into a coaching and advisory role as country capacity grows.develop a network-wide spokesperson methodology: how country teams identify, prepare, support and sustain credible voices over time.build a rapid-response capability so credible local voices can become part of relevant breaking stories in a timely way.create shared infrastructure for narrative testing, media monitoring, intelligence gathering and cross-network learning, so that good practice travels quickly.position och's voices, stories and data for an ai-shaped media environment, including how information is found, summarised, trusted and reused.help country teams map and build relationships with the outlets, validators, think tanks, creators and platforms that reach their audiences.lead on developing crisis response protocolsmanage a budget focused mainly on developing capacity and skills across the networkplan the handover from the start: define the milestones at which central support reduces, what country teams need to demonstrate before taking fuller ownership, and how the function moves to a lighter-touch model.the wider ambitionbeyond the foundational systems, this role carries a larger strategic opportunity. och is well placed to build much needed new public-influence infrastructure. that could include a global or regional network of conservative environmental spokespeople, country-level mapping of the outlets and validators that shape non-progressive audiences, new media partnerships, or even the creation of platforms and formats that engage these audiences seriously. not all of these ideas will prove viable. the postholder will have room to test these ideas, the judgement to decide which are worth pursuing, and the discipline to stop the ones that are not working.what sits with country teamsoch's ethos is rooted in the belief that those closest to the work are best placed to devise and deliver the strategy. the global director of strategic communications will not own national political positioning, decisions about who speaks publicly in each country, campaign priorities and timing, national media relationships, or the specific language of media engagement work in each context.the credibility of the work depends on it being and feeling genuinely local. the role requires authority without directiveness: the ability to set standards, challenge constructively and build capability while leaving ownership where it belongs.person specificationessentialsenior strategic communications judgement. the ability to see how media, politics, audiences, narratives and organisational strategy connect.media-operator credibility. recent, hands-on experience of placing stories, developing spokespeople, managing narratives and working with journalists, editors, creators or platforms at pace.builder instinct. the appetite and ability to create infrastructure from scratch, without an established playbook.coaching orientation. a genuine commitment to developing others' capability rather than defaulting to doing the work personally.political fluency. strong understanding of centre-right and conservative landscapes, and the credibility to engage the validators and spokespeople the network needs to reach.network orchestration. the ability to work across many country contexts, with the cultural judgement to adapt without losing coherence.ai and media change. current, practical interest in how ai is reshaping the way information is produced, found and trusted, and what that means for strategic communications.temperament. the ability to bring authority and judgement, but not ego. able to set clear standards, challenge when needed, and still let country teams own their work.professional proficiency in english (cefr c2 or equivalent).desirableexperience of building, spinning out or scaling a new entity, function or practice.experience of multi-country civil-society networks, international ngos or politically diverse coalitions.experience in climate, environment, energy, land, rural affairs or adjacent public-policy debates.experience working with philanthropic funders, boards or senior political stakeholders.what this role is notthis is not a conventional head of communications role. it is not a content-production function, not a press office, not a brand role for och, and not a command-and-control role directing what country teams say.candidates whose strength lies mainly in running an established communications operation may find the role frustrating. the successful candidate will be someone who wants to build a capability, prove its value, embed it in others and then deliberately let it go.termsreports to: chief strategy officer, working closely with the ceo.team and resources: the postholder will be expected to shape the team, external support and budget required for the build out, in discussion with the ceo and chief strategy officer.hours of work: full-time role. some overlap with european working hours will be helpful during the intensive early phase, when the role works closely with europe-based leadership.what we offera competitive remuneration package, including health insurance, pension contributions and other benefits appropriate to the successful candidate's location.

about primordial labswe're building the next generation interface for commanding autonomous systems in the real world. our core product, anura, translates spoken or typed intent into structured actions across drones, sensors, and mission software—enabling faster, more intuitive control in high-stakes environments. we’re a distributed team of engineers, operators, and technologists focused on deploying reliable autonomy at the tactical edge.the opportunityas the communications manager at primordial labs, you will be the primary architect of our public narrative, ensuring the world understands our technology and the value it brings to our customers. you will work at the intersection of deep tech and national security, turning complex ai products like anura, into compelling messaging for the media, stakeholders, and the warfighter.the role shapes the product narrative, builds relationships with defense, national security, and tech journalists, prepares leadership for interviews and speaking engagements, and supports government affairs, including engaging with hill staff, think tanks, and our ga firms. you’ll work closely with the marketing director to keep messaging consistent across every channel. joining our fully remote team means you’ll have the autonomy to drive high-impact pr strategies while working alongside world-class engineers and former special operators to safeguard national security.what you'll dostrategic storytelling: owning the end to end narrative for our product, helping to craft everything from high-level op-eds to punchy product launch announcements.media relations: building and maintaining deep relationships with top-tier defense trade, national security, and tech journalists to secure high value media placements.executive visibility: preparing our leadership team for interviews, speaking engagements, and industry demos, ensuring our "voice" is consistent and authoritative.policy and government affairs support: shape positioning with hill staff, our lobbying firms, think tanks, and the policy communityintegrated campaigns: collaborating with our marketing, growth, and engineering teams to launch multi-channel campaigns that highlight our mission impact at major events like sof week or ausa.internal & brand comms: keep a growing team aligned on company messaging, news, and external comms policies.about youproven experience: 5+ years in strategic communications, pr, or journalism, specifically within the defense, aerospace, or deep tech sectors.technical translation: ability to take "engineer-speak" and turn it into clear, mission-focused content for non-technical audiences.exceptional writing: mastery of ap style and a track record of crafting tight, memorable narratives under tight deadlines.media savvy: demonstrated success in pitching stories and managing complex media inquiries in a highly regulated industry.preferred qualificationssecurity clearance: an active secret (or higher) security clearance is a major plus.military familiarity: experience working as (or with) a military public affairs officer (pao) or a deep understanding of dod structure.startup agility: experience in a fast-paced "build-fast" environment where you are comfortable being a team of one for all things comms.visual storytelling: basic proficiency in tools like figma, canva, or adobe creative suite to help visualize our tech for social media.important qualification note: due to the nature of our work and federal compliance requirements, this position strictly requires u.s. citizenship and current residency within the united states. please note that permanent residency (green card status) or visa sponsorship cannot satisfy these specific regulatory requirements.compensationcompensation for this position includes a target base salary of $130,000 - $160,000 annually, with the specific figure determined by the candidate's experience level.we’re committed to fair and equitable compensation and are happy to explain how we determine our salary ranges, just ask!our benefitsbeyond a competitive salary, we provide a significant equity stake, aligning your growth with ours.100% remote: this role is fully remote, open to residents across the us. we believe that talent knows no borders (well, except for the us in this case!).comprehensive health coverage: we provide comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans so you and your family can stay healthy and worry free.retirement planning: plan for tomorrow with our 401(k) package, complete with a generous 6% company match.generous dto: our generous discretionary time off (dto) policy is all about helping you take the breaks you deserve and live your healthiest, most fulfilling life.elite technology package: enjoy an elite technology package to make your work effortless and efficient.our interview processour interview process is designed to be thorough and respectful of your time. it typically includes:conversation with the people team: lets get to know one another first!interview: a 45-minute discussion about relevant communications concepts and your past experience.portfolio overview: this session is designed for us to dive into your real-world work, your storytelling approach, and how you translate complex technology into compelling narratives. you’ll walk us through 2–3 case studies or pieces from your past experience that highlight your strategic thinking, messaging skills, and execution across media relations, executive communications, or product announcements.team interviews: collaboration is at the heart of what we do. during this stage, you’ll meet your prospective peers to discuss our team dynamics, project workflows, and how we work together to win.we are committed to a low-stress interview experience—no trick questions or brain teasers!primordial labs is an equal opportunity employer, committed to creating a welcoming and respectful environment for everyone. discrimination and harassment have no place here. we firmly believe that a diverse team enriches our problem-solving capabilities, sparks greater creativity, and ultimately leads to a better product and a more vibrant company.we understand that great talent comes from various paths and that passion and transferable skills are invaluable. at primordial labs, what truly matters is your ability to make an impact, your dedication to our mission, and your capacity to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative atmosphere. we are dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace where you can contribute your unique talents, expand your skills, and learn continuously. if you’re driven to make a real impact, we encourage you to apply, even if your experience doesn’t perfectly align with every qualification.

detail.industry: Accounting, IT Services and IT Consulting, and Business Consulting and Services
detail.desc: do you thrive when developing creative and innovative insights to help organizational leaders solve complex challenges? want to work on research and ideas that reach executive audiences around the world? are you interested in working for a world-class organization that provides an exceptional career experience with an inclusive and collaborative culture? join deloitte's us ethics office to help shape and create data, insights, and analysis on ethical leadership and leading culture practices.work you'll dothe individual in this position is responsible for managing the planning, execution, and effectiveness of external communications for the ethics office. this includes, but is not limited to, drafting or directing thought leadership, social media, and other content related to ethical leadership for the ethics office; building relationships and collaborating with internal and external thought leaders, research professionals, and membership organizations; publishing content in a variety of formats across paid, owned, and earned channels; and recommending creative new formats for reaching audiences and building eminence.recruiting for this role ends on 11/22/2026responsibilities include:drafting and actioning the ethics office external communications/eminence strategy.conducting journalistic research (interviewing internal and external subject-matter resources, conducting desk research, etc.) and/or coordinating with internal and external research providers to apply other research methodologies as appropriate (qual/quant surveys, data analyses, economic modeling, etc.).drafting content pieces resulting from the research and analysis, working with ethics office leaders and others.acting as the storytelling strategist to determine and achieve the optimal storytelling approach to increase audience engagement, and to ensure that each content project is clear and compelling-that the story flows logically and ensures reader/viewer/listener engagement from start to finish, the ideas are well-differentiated and communicated accurately and directly, the phrasing is dynamic and conversational, the overall content project will be perceived by target audiences as high-quality and high-value, and the content will achieve intended objectives.sourcing, engaging, and managing writing contractors, and editing their work.leading and coordinating internal and external stakeholder engagement on timely and future-focused ethical leadership topics and initiatives.collaborating with subject-matter resources to determine the appropriate research, content and channel strategy for each project.managing various ethics office initiatives to elevate the firm's ethics culture and its commitment to integrity and quality.obtaining required reviews for all publications and deliverables.identifying opportunities to incorporate ai across ethics office eminence initiatives.establishing and reviewing metrics to determine the effectiveness of the ethics office's external communications/eminence strategy.supervising, managing performance, and mentoring the career development of other team members.serving as an example to others by operating with the highest level of ethics and integrity.the successful candidate would possess these skills:ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a teameffective written and verbal communication skillsmeticulous attention to detail and quality of work productability to build and sustain professional relationshipsability to lead projects or workstreamsability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environmentstrong interpersonal skills and professional demeanorability to meet deadlinesability to mentor and provide clear guidance to othersthe teamthe ethics office drives deloitte's recognition as a leading voice on ethics, integrity, and speak-up culture in the professional services marketplace, translating that external credibility into the tools, resources, and guidance that help deloitte professionals make sound ethical decisions every day. this dual mandate reflects deloitte's unwavering commitment to ethics and quality as the catalyst for making an impact that matters for our clients, our people, and our communities.qualifications:required:bachelor's degree, preferably in communications, english, marketing, public relations, journalism or related field.7+ years of experience in writing/editing/marketing with a proven track record in creating strategies and fact-based content to intrigue and educate audiences (business journalism and/or data-driven journalism experience preferred).experience using ai.prior experience working on a virtual team.ability to travel up to 20%.must be legally authorized to work in the united states without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.preferred:effective and versatile communication skills, from writing engaging short-form web copy to conducting developmental editing on complex, long-form research reports; experience with creating multimedia content.exceptional writing fluency and knowledge of us english grammar, conversational phrasing, and ap style, and the ability to explain edits to authors.avid consumer of business news and trends, specifically organizational culture and ai.experience in publishing or media.experience producing video/podcasts.experience with corporate research and thought leadership.experience in social media influencing.the wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. the disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. at deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. a reasonable estimate of the current range is $93000 to $191000you may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.ea_exphire,ea_rbp_exphire

detail.desc: small girls pr is seeking a director to lead strategic communications across our growing consumer health and wellness portfolio. in this role, you’ll lead integrated communications strategies for brands shaping how consumers think about and engage with their health and well-being, from emerging disruptors and digital-first platforms to established household names. you’ll develop culturally relevant, consumer-first narratives and campaigns that translate complex health and wellness topics into compelling stories, build brand awareness, and drive meaningful earned media.there is no one-size-fits-all for an sgpr client which means your career will be further enriched with meaningful and diversified experience. we've handled mergers for ge, announced esusu as one of the first black-owned tech unicorns, launched paranormal investigations with ring doorbells, created a closet calculator to see how recycled clothing impacts the environment with thredup, and hired the green m&m as zappos’ newest “shoefluencer” when the spokescandy was put on hiatus due to her boots controversy.note: this role is based in our nyc office, working two days a week in the office on a hybrid schedule. how you'll make an impactdrive strategic vision & proactively identify roadblocks: develop long-term strategies and create tentpole campaigns that position clients for success in competitive markets as well as proactively identify potential roadblocks and solutions in order to ensure client successlead client relationships: build strong rapport with clients and interagency partners as their primary strategic contactgenerate headlines that matter: personally craft compelling pitches, review media lists, and conduct direct outreach to secure feature placements across print, digital, podcasts, substacks, and broadcast publicationsinnovate constantly: originate the out-of-the-box, earned-first ideas that leverage creative thinking to generate tangible results, achieving both client and agency business goalsdeliver measurable results: provide comprehensive insights that capture quantitative outcomes while acknowledging qualitative impactexpand media footprint: develop strategies to consistently secure placements beyond traditional digital outlets as well as outlets clients have never been in beforementor future leaders: guide our talented junior team members to develop their skills and confidence, coaching them on how/when to pivot strategies as well as how to proactively improve internal processeswhat sets you apartpoint positive mindset: you bring realistic optimism to challenges—identifying opportunities without glossing over obstacleshustle and can-do attitude: you're resourceful and nimble, thriving when timelines shift and finding creative solutions when conventional approaches fall shortfuture-forward thinking: your intellectual curiosity drives you to spot emerging trends, tools and communities before they hit the mainstreammedia relations expertise: you've cultivated warm relationships with key journalists and understand how to translate client stories into compelling coverageorganizational excellence: you plan and delegate efficiently, keeping teams focused on priorities even when juggling multiple campaignscreative expertise: you've personally conceived successful pr stunts and campaigns that generated significant attentionqualifications: 7–9+ years of experience in public relations and integrated communications, with significant experience across consumer health, wellness, and lifestyle brandsa strong portfolio of consumer health campaigns that have driven earned media and cultural relevance, with experience translating health, science, or wellness topics into accessible, compelling consumer narrativesdeep understanding of the consumer health and wellness landscape, including emerging trends, shifting consumer behaviors, and the cultural conversations shaping categories such as preventative health, sexual and reproductive health, mental health, nutrition, telehealth, and everyday wellnessestablished relationships with consumer, health, wellness, lifestyle, and business media, with a proven ability to secure meaningful coverage across top-tier national outlets and emerging platformsproven experience developing creative, insight-driven campaigns that bring health and wellness brands into broader consumer and cultural conversationsdemonstrated success leading client relationships and agency teams, with the ability to provide strategic counsel and identify proactive opportunities for brandsstrong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to lead multiple client workstreams and priorities simultaneouslywhy you'll love us:atypical time off: generous pto that scales with tenure, in addition to summer fridays, day of rests for mental health, caregiving days, and time off for unsick days dedicated to preventative caredeep work focus: our smalls in sync program ensures you have dedicated time for collaboration and strategic solo workcomprehensive benefits: a 100% employer-covered medical plan, 401k match up to 4%, dental, vision, and moreinnovation leadership: our agency was amongst the first to offer client brand campaigns on tiktok (back when it was still called musical.ly), has been recognized for pioneering unique hr policies live on the today show, and our ai leadership committee has been training our employees at the intersection of pr and ai for over two years (not two months!)vibrant culture: employee-led committees apply anyway. you may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.we are a diverse and high performing company that is dedicated to creating an inspiring workplace for all. it is the policy of
